title: Sigma-1 Receptor Mitigates Poly-GR-Associated Redox Dysregulation by Restoring NRF2/HO1 Signaling in C9orf72-Associated ALS.
abstract: Hexanucleotide GGGGCC repeat expansions in C9orf72 produce arginine-rich dipeptide repeat proteins, including poly-GR and poly-PR, that contribute to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia. Although poly-GR has been linked to oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, the mechanisms that determine whether antioxidant defenses are preserved or suppressed in poly-GR-expressing motor neurons remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether Sigma-1 receptor (Sigma-1R) modulates poly-GR-associated redox dysregulation in cellular and mouse models. In NSC34 cells, both EGFP-PR42 and EGFP-GR50 expression reduced NRF2 protein levels. EGFP-GR50 expression was also associated with reduced NRF1 and HO1 levels and increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. Sigma-1R overexpression or pharmacological activation with fluvoxamine or PRE084 restored NRF2 and HO1 expression and attenuated both cellular and mitochondrial oxidative stress in EGFP-GR50-expressing cells. Co-treatment with the Sigma-1R antagonist NE100 attenuated the agonist-induced restoration of NRF2 and HO1. Furthermore, the NRF2 inhibitor ML385 attenuated agonist-mediated HO1 restoration, supporting the involvement of NRF2 activity in this downstream response. In an AAV-mediated EGFP-GR50 mouse model, Sigma-1R deficiency was associated with shortened survival, reduced NeuN-positive neuronal counts, and decreased NRF2 immunoreactivity in the brain. Together, these findings identify Sigma-1R as a modulator of poly-GR-associated redox dysregulation and neuronal vulnerability and support further investigation of Sigma-1R modulation as a potential therapeutic strategy for C9orf72-associated ALS.

title: A topographic protomap in mouse subplate neurons precedes the onset of sensory experience.
abstract: Within sensory systems, thalamic projections to layer 4 (L4) neurons establish precise neocortical topography. During development, thalamic axons first synapse onto subplate neurons (SPNs) beneath the cortical plate, however, how thalamic inputs are organized within the subplate is unknown. To examine SPN organization and activity, we generated an inducible Cplx3-CreER mouse driver line to examine SPNs during development. Before sensory onset, we found that Cplx3+ SPNs in the auditory and visual cortices exhibited topographically organized spontaneous activity. Stimulating thalamocortical afferents evoked robust responses in auditory cortex SPNs, indicating functional thalamic input, while cochlear ablation or enucleation dramatically reduced spontaneous activity among Cplx3+ SPNs, indicating that peripherally-generated activity propagates to the subplate. After ear canal opening, Cplx3+ SPNs responded reliably to sound with coarse tonotopy. Thus, Cplx3+ SPNs receive topographically organized input and integrate spontaneous and sensory-driven activity, which may shape refinement of nascent brain circuits.

title: Placental TRPV2 supports trophoblast function and normal fetal development.
abstract: While placental functioning arbitrates fetal outcome, the molecular players that underpin normal placental development remain poorly understood. Here, we provide evidence that the Transient Receptor Potential Vanilloid 2 (TRPV2) channel plays an important role in normal placental development, determining fetal size and survival. Its absence severely affects placental morphology, causing fetal growth restriction and embryonic lethality, which was found to be allocated to a non-redundant role in the trophoblast, but not in the embryo. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated Trpv2 deletion in mouse trophoblast stem cells demonstrated that Trpv2 contributes to the differentiation towards Syncytiotrophoblast layer II (SynTII) cells, which was confirmed by the growth restriction phenotype in SynTII-specific Trpv2 knockout animals. Finally, TRPV2 was functionally expressed in human trophoblast cells and enriched in trophoblast populations undergoing syncytial differentiation. Together, our findings identify an important role for TRPV2 during placental development and consequently fetal outcomes.

title: ROS-autocatalytic nanoplatform interfering astrocyte-cancer crosstalk and enhancing glioblastoma therapy.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains incurable and exhibits exceptionally high metabolic demands, driving the evolution of hyperactive mitochondrial systems within tumors. In parallel, mitochondrial transfer from astrocytes to cancer cells fuels metabolic reprogramming and enhances GBM tumorigenicity. These malignant traits markedly constrain therapeutic efficacy and patient survival. Herein, we report a dehydroascorbic acid (DHA)-functionalized, ROS-responsive, ferrocene-integrated polymer nanoplatform (GS@DFP) co-loaded with S-Gboxin and Galunisertib, simultaneously targeting GBM mitochondria and mitochondrial transfer in astrocyte-cancer cell crosstalk. After crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) through Glut1-mediated transport enabled by DHA, GS@DFP responds to elevated intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in GBM to trigger payload release and initiate Fenton reactions. S-Gboxin inhibits mitochondrial complex V and depletes ATP, whereas Galunisertib downregulates TGF-β/SMAD-driven thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1) expression, suppressing tumor microtube (MT) formation and thereby reducing astrocyte-to-GBM mitochondrial transfer. Notably, TGF-β inhibition also reprograms the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). This work establishes a multifunctional nanoplatform that targets mitochondrial vulnerabilities and intercellular crosstalk, offering a translatable strategy for enhancing GBM therapy.

title: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor use and risk of neurodegenerative disease: A Swedish population-based cohort study.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Effective disease-modifying therapies remain unavailable for neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs). Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) indicated for chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) have been hypothesized to modulate the pathological mechanisms underlying neurodegeneration. Therefore, we aimed to explore the association between initiation of six different TKIs and the subsequent risk of developing NDDs in Swedish nationwide registries (2005-2024). CML patients ≥50 years at diagnosis initiating TKI therapy were identified, alongside five comparators without CML matched on sex, age, and residence at diagnosis. CML cases and comparators were followed from the initiation date of the respective TKI and could contribute follow-up time to multiple TKI cohorts. A composite measure of NDD diagnosis or death due to NDD was the outcome. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models, with adjustments for calendar year at follow-up initiation, and relevant comorbidities. A total of 1322 CML cases were included in the study. 1188 initiated imatinib (of which 41 experienced an NDD event), 541 dasatinib (15 events), 390 nilotinib (five events), 174 bosutinib, 71 ponatinib, and 41 asciminib. Adjusted hazard ratios comparing each TKI group to their matched comparator populations were 0.98 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.71 to 1.36) for imatinib users, 1.18 (95% CI, 0.68 to 2.03) for dasatinib users, and 0.37 (95% CI, 0.15 to 0.90) for nilotinib users. Bosutinib, ponatinib, and asciminib users were too few to conduct comparative analyses. Initiation of nilotinib, but not imatinib or dasatinib, was associated with a significantly lower NDD incidence relative to general population comparators.

title: Data‑driven cognitive composites predict Aβ‑related decline and progression to MCI: the ADOPIC study.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Cognitive composites offer greater sensitivity to amyloid beta (Aβ)-related decline compared to individual tests for tracking longitudinal cognitive change. We developed and validated data-driven composites from the harmonized Alzheimer's Dementia Onset and Progression in International Cohorts (ADOPIC) study, addressing gaps in psychometric reporting and multi-cohort validation. The study included 1964 cognitively unimpaired (CU) participants at baseline (longitudinal subset = 1110). Principal component analysis-derived domain-specific and general cognitive composites were evaluated for psychometric properties, sensitivity to Aβ-related decline, and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) progression prediction compared to the Alzheimer's Disease Cooperative Study - Preclinical Alzheimer's Cognitive Composite (ADCS-PACC). Proposed composites demonstrated good to excellent psychometric properties and sensitivity to differentiating CU Aβ trajectories (p < 0.001). General cognition demonstrated longitudinal sensitivity comparable to the ADCS-PACC (d = -0.20) and equivalent classification performance (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.70). All composites significantly predicted MCI progression (p < 0.001). The composites perform comparably to the ADCS-PACC, developed for CU with Aβ, in longitudinal sensitivity while providing comprehensive psychometric characterization and domain-specific measurement, supporting their utility as outcome measures in preclinical Alzheimer's disease studies.

title: In memoriam: A tribute to Marie J. Gibson, PhD.
Sputum and oral microbiota profiles are associated with long COVID severity and phenotype post-hospitalisation: a UK multicentre, prospective cohort study.
abstract: Acute COVID-19 alters the airway microbiota. Whether these changes persist post-COVID-19 and contribute to long COVID is unknown. We aimed to describe the microbiota by long COVID severity and subtype, and identify links with inflammation. Adults were prospectively recruited to the longitudinal UK Post-hospitalisation COVID-19 study (PHOSP-COVID). Patients were grouped by previously described "severity clusters" (of ongoing health impairments) and symptom subgroups. Oral and sputum microbiota (at 6 months post-discharge) were characterised through 16S ribosomal RNA gene amplicon sequencing, and microbiota diversity was assessed. Co-occurrence network analysis identified keystone taxa. Associations between keystone taxa and plasma inflammatory proteins were assessed through Spearman's rank correlations. 771 participants had their microbiota assessed. Of participants with oral rinses and "severity cluster" assignment (mean age 57.5 years), 278 out of 722 (38.5%) were women. The "very severe" cluster, in which disease was predominantly pulmonary in nature, was associated with a distinct microbiota profile post-COVID-19. Reduced lung function was associated with a distinct oral microbiota profile. Persistent neurocognitive symptoms were associated with a distinct oral microbiota profile, while gastrointestinal symptoms were associated with a distinct sputum microbiota profile. Microbiota keystone taxa shifted to a higher prevalence of lactic acid bacteria associated with worse health outcomes. Lactic acid bacteria abundance was associated with elevated blood inflammatory proteins. Distinct oral and sputum microbiota profiles were associated with pulmonary function and with neurocognitive and gastrointestinal symptoms in long COVID. Shifts in keystone microbiota taxa linked with inflammation, based on worse health outcomes, suggest a potential role change for lactic acid bacteria, which may be associated with the host immune response.

title: KIF1A c.773C > T impairs neural progenitor differentiation and axonal transport in association with dysregulated Wnt/β-catenin-BDNF signaling.
abstract: Pathogenic KIF1A variants are established cause neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders. However, the mechanisms by which they perturb early human neural development remains undefined. Here, we identified a heterozygous KIF1A c.773C > T (p.T258M) mutation in a Chinese family with hereditary spastic paraplegia and modeled its pathogenicity using patient-derived iPSCs and CRISPR-Cas9-corrected isogenic controls. We found that KIF1A-mutant neural stem cells (NSCs) exhibited hyperproliferation, impaired cell-cycle exit, and defective neuronal differentiation, accompanied by defective neurite outgrowth, neuronal complexity, and calcium activity. Mechanistically, the KIF1A c.773C > T mutation compromised the binding affinity of KIF1A for β-tubulin and thereby impaired microtubule-associated localization of BDNF and synaptophysin. Integrated transcriptomic and biochemical analyses further revealed dysregulation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Notably, pharmacological activation of Wnt signaling restored BDNF expression, whereas exogenous BDNF rescued the proliferative and differentiative defects, indicating a potential functional relationship between BDNF and Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Collectively, these findings suggested that dysregulated Wnt/β-catenin-BDNF signaling may serve as a contributory mechanism linking KIF1A motor dysfunction to aberrant neural stem cell fate.

title: NUP35 drives the Warburg effect and malignant progression in glioblastoma by regulating GCKR stability and HK2 activation.
abstract: The Warburg effect drives glioblastoma (GBM) progression, but its upstream regulators remain unclear. This study investigated the role and mechanism of nucleoporin 35 (NUP35) in GBM glycolytic reprogramming. Public datasets, including The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) database, were analyzed to identify glycolysis-related genes in GBM. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses were performed. NUP35 gain- and loss-of-function models were used to assess glycolysis, HK2 activity, lactate production, apoptosis, invasion, and tumor growth. Co-immunoprecipitation, ubiquitination, protein stability, and molecular docking assays were used to explore the mechanism. Bioinformatics analyses identified NUP35 as a key glycolysis-associated molecule that was markedly upregulated in GBM tissues and significantly associated with poor clinical outcomes. Functional enrichment analyses demonstrated that NUP35-related genes were predominantly enriched in glycolytic metabolism, energy metabolism, and tumor progression-associated signaling pathways. Functional experiments further showed that NUP35 enhanced glycolytic reprogramming by increasing HK2 activity and lactate production, thereby promoting GBM cell invasion, suppressing apoptosis, and accelerating tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, NUP35 regulated GCKR protein abundance without altering GCKR transcription. TRIM25 interacted with GCKR, and TRIM25 knockdown or expression of the GCKR-K525A mutant reduced GCKR ubiquitination and restored total GCKR protein levels in NUP35-overexpressing cells. These findings support a requirement for TRIM25 and the K525 residue of GCKR in GCKR ubiquitination and degradation under NUP35-overexpressing conditions, with consequent changes in HK2 activity and glycolytic metabolism. NUP35 promotes glycolytic reprogramming and malignant progression in GBM by regulating GCKR protein stability and HK2 activity. TRIM25 is required for GCKR ubiquitination and degradation under NUP35-overexpressing conditions, supporting a proposed NUP35-TRIM25-GCKR-HK2 regulatory model.

title: Anti-inflammatory IL-4 shapes the architecture of presynaptic glutamatergic puncta of human and murine sensory neurons for pain sensitivity.
abstract: The pleiotropic anti-inflammatory cytokine interleukin 4 (IL-4) not only modulates immune responses but also plays important roles in the nervous system by mediating itch, antinociception and neuroregeneration. Here, we assessed the expression and function of IL-4, its receptors, and downstream signaling pathways in human induced pluripotent stem cell derived nociceptors (iNocs), organotypic mouse spinal cord cultures, and in in vivo models. In silico analyses of human and mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) single cell transcriptomes revealed that a specific subpopulation of murine and human sensory neurons expressed IL4R and IL13RA1 (but very little IL2RG) receptor subunits highlighting conserved neuron responsiveness to IL-4. In iNocs, exogenous IL-4 induced de novo formation of presynaptic vGLUT1-positive puncta. Pharmacological inhibition of Janus kinases 1/2, STAT6, protein kinase C isoforms, or the translation initiation factor eIF4E significantly attenuated the IL-4-associated increase in vGLUT1-positive puncta. Transcriptomic profiling of iNocs revealed IL-4-regulated biological processes associated with neuronal development and synaptic organization. Consistently, IL-4 increased mean-firing-rate in iNocs and increased vGLUT1 expression in mouse organotypic spinal cord cultures treated with IL-4, in vitro. Intrathecal or intranasal IL-4 treatment enhanced both, inhibitory and excitatory synaptic activity in acute spinal cord slices, and this was associated with a decrease in mechanical and thermal sensitivity but normal sensorimotor coordination in vivo. These findings position IL-4 as key regulator of presynaptic glutamatergic organization for primary afferent neuron connectivity in the spinal dorsal horn and support a critical role for IL-4 in the excitation - inhibition balance of pain processing spinal neuronal networks.

title: Age-dependent brain mechanics are linked to microstructural changes.
abstract: Accurate knowledge of brain tissue mechanics is essential for understanding the pathologies that cause mechanical changes and for developing reliable computer models for neurosurgical procedures. However, the age-related changes in brain mechanics and their microstructural basis are not fully understood. In this study, we examined age-related changes in brain mechanics and microstructure in porcine tissue across five age groups, from early development to young adulthood. Mechanical tests in tension and compression were performed in different anatomical regions, including an anisotropic characterization of the corpus callosum. We used Bayesian parameter identification to estimate material parameters based on isotropic, hyperelastic Ogden and anisotropic, hyperelastic Gasser-Ogden-Holzapfel models under the assumption of large deformations with finite strains. Histological analyses additionally quantified myelin, cell, glia, and neuron measures. Our results revealed nonlinear age dependencies of tensile and compressive mechanics accompanied by clear age-dependent microstructural differences. Notably, myelin- and glia-related measures were the most consistent positive correlates of stiffness. Further, mediation analysis suggested that microstructure, particularly glia-related features, may serve as a measurable intermediate link between age and mechanics. These findings provide a microstructurally informed basis for more realistic, age-dependent computational brain models. Statement of Significance: In order to develop realistic computational models of the brain, it is essential to understand why brain mechanics change with age. While previous work has described age-dependent mechanical behavior, the structural basis of these changes remains unclear. In this study, we combine previously published mechanical data with new, sample-specific histological measurements across development. The key innovation is the use of mediation analysis to test for a measurable statistical link between microstructural changes and mechanics while accounting for the direct effect of age. This approach provides more mechanistic insight than age-dependent mechanical characterization or simple correlation alone. It also helps identify which tissue components are most relevant for explaining developmental changes in brain mechanics.

title: Isoform differentiation studies of arginase: From structural function to design strategies for specific ligands and their application prospects.
abstract: Arginase (ARG), a binuclear manganese metalloenzyme, hydrolyzes L-arginine to L-ornithine and urea, competitively regulating NO bioavailability with NOS. Mammals express two isoforms, ARG1 (cytosolic) and ARG2 (mitochondrial), that share a conserved catalytic core yet exert distinct physiological and pathological effects. ARG1 is essential for hepatic urea detoxification, as systemic Arg1 knockout mice develop hyperammonemia within 10-12 days after birth; in contrast, Arg2 knockout mice show only slightly elevated plasma arginine levels with no overt phenotypic abnormalities, this significant difference highlights the importance of a thorough analysis of the functional divergence between ARG1 and ARG2. Pathologically, ARG1 drives immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment, promotes vascular dysfunction in hypertension and atherosclerosis, and contributes to fibrotic remodeling; ARG2 fuels M1 macrophage inflammatory responses, modulates mitochondrial metabolism, and participates in neurodegeneration. This review systematically examines isoform differences across four dimensions: structural-functional divergence, localization-driven functional segregation, differential pathological contributions, and the current landscape of isoform-selective inhibitors. We further discuss rational design strategies for specific ligands and highlight the translational prospects of isoform-targeted therapies. Exploiting ARG1/ARG2 differentiation represents a promising avenue for precision intervention in cancer, cardiovascular disease, inflammation, and neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Trait anxiety is associated with anxious anticipation and altered perceptions of physiological arousal during acute psychological stress.
abstract: Individuals with higher trait anxiety report more anticipatory anxiety prior to stressful events. In general, experiences of acute stressful events are associated with increases in both actual physiological arousal (i.e., heart rate) and perceptions of physiological arousal (i.e., perceived heart rate changes). However, whether trait anxiety is associated with anticipatory anxiety which in turn is associated with subsequent alterations in perceived and actual physiological arousal during stress has not yet been explored. Young adults (N = 421, 62.7% Female) completed a standardized acute psychological stress task. Participants reported their anticipatory cognitive and somatic anxiety intensity levels after the task instructions but before beginning the stress task. Immediately after the stress task, participants reported their perceived stressor-evoked physiological arousal intensity. Participants also completed a measure of trait anxiety. Heart rate was measured continuously via electrocardiogram during baseline and the stress task. Higher trait anxiety was associated with increased levels of anticipatory cognitive anxiety and somatic anxiety intensity, and cognitive and somatic anticipatory anxiety intensity, in turn, were associated with greater perceived physiological arousal. In contrast, anticipatory anxiety intensity was not associated with actual heart rate reactivity. Results demonstrated that individuals with elevated trait anxiety experienced more anxious anticipation of a stressor, which relates to a potential discrepancy in perceptions verses actual cardiac responses to the stressor.

title: Clocks and steroids interaction across the life span.
abstract: The circadian system enables organisms to anticipate daily environmental changes and to align physiology and behaviour with the external light-dark cycle. In mammals, this temporal organisation is coordinated by the central pacemaker in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), which synchronises peripheral clocks through humoral and neural signals throughout the body. The circadian clock and steroid hormones are linked through a reciprocal, multi-level regulatory relationship. While the SCN and peripheral clocks shape the temporal pattern of steroid secretion, steroid hormones feed back onto the SCN and peripheral clocks, thereby modifying clock gene expression, phase, amplitude, synchrony, and network coherence. This interaction is dynamic across the lifespan, as both the clock and the steroid environment change during development, reproductive life, and ageing. During prenatal and early postnatal development, maternal glucocorticoids (GCs) and other perinatal steroid signals provide time-dependent cues that may shape the maturation and long-term function of the circadian system. During reproductive life in females, ovarian steroids dynamically remodel clocks within the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis, coordinating reproductive timing with circadian signals from the SCN. In parallel, GCs interact with the reproductive axis and may influence fertility in a time-of-day- and cycle-stage-dependent manner. Disruption of this temporal coordination, for example, by shift work, may impair reproductive and endocrine function. With advancing age, both circadian and endocrine rhythms lose robustness, leading to weakened coordination between the SCN and peripheral clocks, as well as reduced synchrony among cellular clocks within peripheral tissues. These changes contribute to disturbed sleep-wake rhythms, reproductive ageing, and altered stress responsiveness. This review discusses the interaction between steroid hormones and circadian clocks across the life span, highlighting reciprocal regulation as a key mechanism linking temporal organisation to physiology and health.

title: Ontogenetic consequences of developmental temperature in amphibians: simultaneous gains in heat tolerance and cumulative costs to stress physiology.
abstract: Heat tolerance is critical for ectotherms facing environmental temperature variability, yet how it varies across life stages, and whether trade-offs occur between temperature-induced developmental plasticity and heat tolerance, remain unclear, particularly in organisms undergoing metamorphosis which represent 95% of all animal species. We examined how early-life thermal conditions shape growth, development, survival, acclimation capacity, heat tolerance, and energy allocation across ontogeny in the African clawed frog (Xenopus laevis), reared at six constant temperatures (17-32°C). We tested whether higher developmental temperatures generate trade-offs between accelerated growth and heat tolerance, and the consequences for post-metamorphic resilience to extreme heat. Rearing at 32°C was lethal before metamorphosis. At non-lethal warm temperatures (17-29°C), larvae and juveniles simultaneously accelerated development, maintained growth, and enhanced heat tolerance. However, juveniles reared at 29°C showed reduced survival, elevated corticosterone responses to acute stress, and diminished acclimation capacity, indicating increased energetic demands and constrained metabolic flexibility. These findings show that amphibians can integrate developmental plasticity with plastic adjustments in heat tolerance, but that such strategies incur cumulative physiological costs. By adopting an across-life-stage approach, our study highlights energy-allocation constraints that may limit population persistence under climate warming in species with complex life cycles.

title: Generation of a human induced pluripotent stem cell line (PNUYHi004-A) from a patient with hereditary spastic paraplegia type 46 (SPG46) carrying compound heterozygous GBA2 variants.
abstract: SPG46 is a rare autosomal recessive form of hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in GBA2, encoding the non-lysosomal glucosylceramidase. We generated an induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) line from peripheral blood mononuclear cells of a 40-year-old Korean patient with adult-onset complicated HSP carrying novel compound heterozygous GBA2 variants (NM_020944.3: c.2059_2072del, p.Tyr687ValfsTer23; c.2621C > T, p.Ser874Leu), using non-integrating Sendai virus vectors. The iPSC line showed a normal karyotype, expressed markers of undifferentiated hPSC, and differentiated into all three germ layers. This line provides a resource for studying GBA2-associated SPG46 and sphingolipid-related neurodegeneration.

title: Reference frame for Adult Brainstem gliomas.
abstract: Brainstem gliomas (BSG) are rare in adults (less than 2% of all gliomas) and generally have a better prognosis than pediatric BSG, although outcomes remain heterogeneous. Many other central nervous system (CNS) tumors, as well as nontumoral lesions, have been described as differential diagnoses and should be kept in mind. Each case should be examined by neurosurgeons from specialized centers to determine the most appropriate surgical approach among stereotactic biopsy, open biopsy, and tumor resection. Surgery may sometimes be performed in expert centers. The main objectives of tumor tissue sampling are to perform histomolecular analyses to confirm the diagnosis, determine the tumor subtype, and identify potential prognostic and theranostic biomarkers. Tissue preservation is essential to ensure that sufficient tumor material is available for further molecular analyses for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Results of ctDNA detection in CSF should only be considered if they are positive. The management of BSGs in adults remains non-standardized, largely because most glioma trials exclude tumors located in this specific site. To date, no prospective trials have established clear treatment guidelines, and most of the available data come from retrospective studies or extrapolation of data from other locations. Radiotherapy (RT) is one of the main treatment options for BSGs in adults. The role of chemotherapy remains unclear due to limited data in literature and is currently being studied. Several molecular targets with therapeutic potential, including recurrent genetic mutations and fusion transcripts, have been identified in adult BSGs.

title: Multiple stressor effects of hypoxia and metals on ventilation, activity, bioaccumulation, and loss of equilibrium in fathead minnows.
abstract: Hypoxia is an increasing concern in freshwater ecosystems, driven by warming, stratification, and nutrient enrichment. Fish cope with hypoxia through behavioural and ventilatory adjustments, yet growing evidence suggests that certain metals can impair these critical compensatory mechanisms. It is currently unknown whether lead (Pb) and nickel (Ni), released in part through expanding mining operations, may alter these critical survival responses. We tested whether 48 hr Pb and Ni exposure impaired fathead minnows' (Pimephales promelas) responses to hypoxia by measuring their gill metal accumulation, ventilation rates, behaviour (movement), and hypoxia tolerance (as measured by % dissolved oxygen [DO] at loss-of-equilibrium [LOE]). Notably, Pb (43 μg/L) exposure during hypoxia resulted in 3.5 × greater gill bioaccumulation, indicating changes in gill uptake dynamics. Opercular movements were used as a proxy for the hypoxic ventilatory response (HVR) and the increase in ventilation in Ni exposed fish was 48% less than the increase in unexposed fish, indicating a blunted HVR. Ni (318 μg/L) increased fish activity, as measured by total distance moved, in both normoxia and hypoxia. Both metals increased hypoxia tolerance as measured by LOE. Together, it appears that co-exposure to Pb and hypoxia may increase gill Pb accumulation due to a maintained HVR, and short-term exposure to Ni can increase locomotion, without affecting ventilatory responses to hypoxia. These results underscore the importance of multiple-stressor research to better understand the interplay of hypoxia and metals to inform water quality guidelines.

title: Perfusion quality does not necessarily predict ultrastructural preservation after hyperosmotic brain perfusion.
abstract: Perfusion fixation is widely used in neuroscience to prepare mammalian brain tissue for histological and ultrastructural analysis. Perfusion protocols are commonly assessed using macroscopic indicators such as gross appearance and neuroimaging, which assess the extent to which perfusate has been distributed throughout the brain. There is a critical need to determine to what extent these metrics can accurately predict high-quality ultrastructural preservation, particularly as new perfusion protocols are developed for connectomics. In this technical report, we describe evidence that these two measures can be decoupled by the addition of dehydrating agents to the perfusate solution. In three human brain donors and one canine brain donor perfused with a fixative solution containing 10% mannitol and 10% polyethylene glycol 35 kDa, macroscopic and radiological indicators of perfusion quality appeared adequate or favorable. However, electron microscopy revealed expanded extracellular space, shrunken cellular processes, and distorted cell membranes, consistent with an osmotic shock artifact resulting from severe hyperosmotic dehydration. Similar ultrastructural artifacts were observed in a canine brain donor perfused with 20% mannitol in 20% neutral buffered formalin without PEG. We compare these ultrastructural findings with findings from previously reported cases perfused with standard neutral buffered formalin without osmotic additives. These findings illustrate a risk of optimizing brain perfusion protocols designed to preserve neural circuitry based on macroscopic or radiological perfusion quality metrics alone, since these metrics can be satisfied while the ultrastructure is severely compromised.

title: Effect Size Calculation Procedures in Exercise Intervention Meta-Analyses: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Meta-analyses require the calculation of effect sizes for all included studies. The most common experimental design in exercise intervention studies is the pre-post control design. A number of different approaches exist for calculating effect sizes for this design, and it is currently unknown which calculation methods are actually used in the published exercise science literature and how this might impact results. We extracted all meta-analyses (N = 101) published in six journals over a 2-year period where the primary studies used a pre-post control design. We recalculated randomly selected primary study effect sizes in each meta-analysis to determine the calculation methods used and compare them to the reported methods. An example case was used to illustrate the impact of using different calculation methods on meta-analysis outcomes. We identified a total of 50 unique combinations of calculation methods among the n = 91 meta-analyses for which we could determine the calculation procedure. Most researchers used change score-based standardized mean differences. These required the imputation of a pre-post correlation, for which most authors used fixed benchmarks instead of evidence-based or previously reported values. Reporting was often incomplete and we identified major issues in the calculation of at least 27 articles. We demonstrate that different calculation methods can yield different meta-analysis outcomes. Effect size calculation procedures vary widely, which can affect meta-analysis outcomes and mislead their interpretation. A considerable number of published meta-analytical findings in exercise science may differ when other reasonable or corrected calculation methods are used. We provide recommendations on how to choose an appropriate effect size method for the pre-post control design. We encourage researchers to transparently report and justify the procedures used and perform sensitivity analyses when performing meta-analyses.

title: An update on neuro-otology and neuro-ophthalmology - focusing on new developments in the last three years.
abstract: Vertigo, dizziness, and imbalance are among the most frequent presenting symptoms in primary care and in the emergency department (ED). The clinical diagnosis is based on a structured patient history and bedside examination of the vestibular system and the ocular motor system, looking especially for central ocular motor signs. Recent guidelines, such as the GRACE-3 guideline on acute vertigo and dizziness, the increasing availability of bedside diagnostic algorithms, and the use of quantitative vestibular and ocular motor testing in both the ED-setting and in the outpatient center have facilitated and standardized the approach to the dizzy patient. Here we review recent developments in neuro-otology and neuro-ophthalmology, covering the period after the latest neuro-otology update was published in this journal in 2023. Both new-onset acute, episodic and chronic vestibular conditions are discussed separately, highlighting advancements in disease characterization, diagnostic criteria, and treatment strategies. While major progress has been made in terms of the pathophysiology, etiology, genetics, and diagnostic criteria of peripheral, central, and functional vestibular diseases as well as ocular motor disorders, this knowledge has to be transferred into clinical practice. Systematic teaching of doctors to increase knowledge and to improve skills in applying the different tests in clinical practice on a high level are identified challenges. In terms of treatment, there is still a very great need for state-of-the art clinical trials applying approved therapies.

title: Osteoporosis risk in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma using muscarinic and prostaglandin agonists: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BackgroundGlaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) arising as the most common subtype. Recent studies have shown that muscarinic and prostaglandin pathways can modulate bone remodeling under systemic, context-dependent conditions. M3 muscarinic receptor activation has been linked to increased bone formation and decreased resorption, whereas continuous prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) administration inhibits bone resorption, with intermittent use inducing bone formation. Given the minimal systemic findings of topical ophthalmic medications, the clinical relevance of bone remodeling effects for patients treated with glaucoma eye drops, particularly in regard to osteoporosis, remains uncertain and warrants evaluation.Patients and MethodsA retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX network with approximately 100 million de-identified electronic medical records. Cohorts included POAG patients prescribed either prostaglandin analogs (e.g. latanoprost, bimatoprost, travoprost, tafluprost) without muscarinic agonist use, or muscarinic M3 agonists (e.g. pilocarpine, carbachol) without prostaglandin analog use. Propensity score matching was performed for age, sex, comorbidities, and concurrent glaucoma medications to limit possible cofounders. The outcome was defined as a diagnosis of osteoporosis without current pathological fracture (ICD code M81). Risk ratios (RR), odd ratios (OR), and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated.ResultsAfter matching, each cohort included 6,743 patients. The incidence of osteoporosis is 13.3% in the prostaglandin cohort and 8.9% in the muscarinic cohort. Prostaglandin agonist use was associated with a statistically significant increase in osteoporosis risk (RR = 0.67, 95% CI 0.60-0.73; OR = 0.63, 95% CI 0.57-0.71; p < 0.0001).ConclusionProstaglandin agonist use was associated with an increased risk of osteoporosis compared with muscarinic agonist therapy in POAG patients. These findings suggest potential systemic effects (e.g. changes to bone health) of prostaglandin agonist use beyond previously known local, ocular effects and highlight the importance of considering osteoporosis risk in glaucoma management.

title: Population-based incidence rate of in-hospital delirium in older adults in Norway-a HUNT study.
abstract: Most studies of delirium occurrence are based on selected hospitalised populations or administrative data. We aimed to estimate the incidence rate of in-hospital delirium in older adults and to assess use of the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) delirium code (F05) in electronic health records. This population-based cohort study included 9956 participants aged ≥70 years from HUNT4 70+. Participants were followed from the date of study participation (2017-19) until 31 December 2023. In-hospital delirium was identified by retrospective chart review of all admissions during follow-up, using Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, fifth edition criteria. Incidence rates were estimated using the first delirium episode per participant, weighted for non-participation. During follow-up, 1507 participants (15.1%) experienced ≥1 in-hospital delirium episode. The weighted incidence rate was 33.1 (95% CI 31.5-34.9) per 1000 person-years and increased with age from 11.4 (age 70-74) to 109.0 (age ≥90) per 1000 person-years. Men had higher incidence rates than women across age groups. Among admissions with delirium, 11.9% had an ICD-10 discharge delirium diagnosis code (F05). In-hospital delirium was common, increased markedly with age and was rarely captured by diagnostic coding. Low coding rates suggest that routine health-care data substantially underestimate delirium burden. Under-recognition of delirium may limit opportunities for follow-up in a group at high risk of adverse outcomes. With an ageing population, the burden of delirium is likely to increase for individuals and health-care systems. Our findings support systematic approaches to improve identification and management.

title: Long-term survival of autologous peripheral nerve fascicles transplanted into the substantia nigra of participants with Parkinson disease: Preliminary observations.
abstract: Cell transplantation therapies for Parkinson disease (PD) require confirmation that grafted tissue withstands the degenerative environment of the diseased brain. Autologous peripheral nerve tissue (PNT) grafts transplanted into the substantia nigra (SN) have been investigated in an ongoing clinical program, but characterization of graft survival after extended periods in the human CNS has been limited. We present histological and immunohistochemical analysis of PNT grafts in postmortem tissue from two participants who lived 7 years 11 months and 9 years 2 months following transplantation. Grafts persisted as structurally organized tissue with preserved fascicular architecture, compartmentalized boundaries defined by convergent GFAP-negative and COL1A1-positive demarcation, and cellular density comparable to naïve sural nerve. Immune cell presence within grafts was limited (4-7%) and concentrated at graft-host interfaces. Vascular networks including CD31-positive capillaries and SMA-positive arterioles were identified within grafts. Transplanted tissue maintained PNS identity with Schwann cell markers p75NTR, S100B, and MPZ detected within grafts, contrasting MBP expression in surrounding parenchyma. TH-positive processes within grafts, spatially associated with MPZ immunoreactivity, supported interactions between grafted Schwann cells and catecholaminergic processes consistent with dopaminergic origin. These findings provide histological evidence that autologous PNT grafts persist as organized, cellularly viable, transplanted tissue with maintained PNS identity after extended survival in the parkinsonian SN.

title: Retrospective Registration and Completer-Only Analysis Limit Confirmatory Claims of SRAM Superiority in Cervical Spondylosis [Letter].
Connected Care: Challenges and Potential of Digital Interventions in Substance Use Disorder - a Narrative Review.
abstract: mHealth interventions have demonstrated positive outcomes across various health domains and represent promising tools for supporting the treatment of Substance Use Disorders (SUD). However, gaps remain regarding user and clinician engagement, factors associated with positive outcomes, and the need for cultural adaptation. To analyze recent literature on the effectiveness of mHealth interventions in the treatment of SUD, identifying interaction patterns and functionalities that promote adherence in diverse contexts. A narrative review was conducted based on PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching PUBMED, SCOPUS, EMBASE and WEB OF SCIENCE for English-language articles published between 2014 and 2024. The review focused on barriers, facilitators, and the effectiveness of implementing digital interventions (mHealth) in the management of SUD. Of the 593 articles identified, 34 were included. Despite considerable heterogeneity in evaluated outcomes, digital interventions demonstrated positive impacts on smoking cessation, contingency management for opioids, and reduction in alcohol and cannabis use. Notably, response variability was observed according to cultural and generational differences, severity of use, substance type, and digital literacy. Additional challenges include long-term adherence and a scarcity of studies in low- and middle-income countries. Digital interventions show tangible clinical benefits across multiple substances, with usability and connected care driving sustained engagement. The use of mHealth, particularly as a complementary and combined approach in treating individuals with SUD, is associated with clinical and accessibility benefits. However, further research is required to evaluate its applicability across diverse populations and contexts.

title: 3D-Printed Models as Catalysts for Neuroanatomy Learning: An Immersive Educational Experience for Medical Students.
abstract: Introduction Neuroanatomy presents unique challenges due to the three-dimensional (3D) complexity of the nervous system. This study evaluates the impact of 3D-printed brainstem models on neuroanatomy teaching to medical students. Methods A descriptive, cross-sectional, non-randomized, between-group study was conducted to compare students' perceptions of 3D-printed anatomical models versus traditional schematic diagrams. Participants were recruited through non-probability convenience sampling and allocated to a 3D-model group (n = 38) or a traditional-diagram group (n = 23). A Likert-type questionnaire assessed perceived motivation, clarity, understanding, usefulness, and satisfaction. Descriptive statistics and the Mann-Whitney U test were used for between-group comparisons. Results Sixty-one responses were analyzed. Compared with traditional schematic diagrams, 3D-printed models received significantly higher ratings for conceptual clarity, overall satisfaction, and preference for future use (p < 0.05). In contrast, schematic diagrams received higher ratings for motivation, a finding that may reflect unmeasured factors such as prior familiarity with conventional learning resources. Conclusions The use of 3D printing improves the neuroanatomical learning experience for medical students, as it is perceived as an innovative, clear, and complementary resource. Its implementation can transform traditional neuroscience teaching.

title: Hepatic HIF2α Modulates Extra-Hepatic Disease-Associated Phenotypes During Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) afflicts more than one-third of adults globally, contributing significantly to an increased cardiovascular disease risk. Further, patients with severe liver disease experience muscle weakness and fatigue. Hypoxia-inducible factor 2α (HIF2α) accumulates in the livers of MASLD patients. Here we sought to understand the role of hepatic HIF2α in mediating hepatic and extra-hepatic features of MASLD. Using an obese mouse model of MASLD, we investigated the impact of hepatocyte-specific HIF2α deletion (hHIF2α-/-) on hepatic, cardiac and skeletal muscle metabolism, and cardiac function. Over 28 weeks, mice were exposed to a high-fat, high-fructose, high-cholesterol (GAN) diet, which induced obesity, hepatic steatosis, fibrosis and inflammation. hHIF2α-/- was associated with greater hepatic NADH-supported mitochondrial respiration, higher sphingomyelin levels and protection against MASLD induced hyperinsulinaemia, but not against hepatic manifestations of MASLD. Instead, in the hearts of GAN-fed mice, hHIF2α-/- caused diacylglycerol and long-chain acyl-carnitine accumulation and exacerbated diet-induced ceramide accumulation. Langendorff-perfused hearts from hHIF2α-/- mice showed systolic and diastolic dysfunction, including 24% lower left ventricular developed pressure and 34% lower maximal rate of relaxation (dP/dtmin). However, isolated hearts from hHIF2α-/- mice were protected against MASLD-associated sympathetic dominance, determined using autonomic receptor agonist stimulation. Both GAN-feeding and hHIF2α-/- were associated with lower lean mass (14% and 5.4% lower than respective controls), whilst hHIF2α-/- enhanced OXPHOS-associated protein levels in gastrocnemius muscle. Overall, hHIF2α-/- resulted in detrimental extra-hepatic effects, including myocardial lipid accumulation, impaired cardiac function, and loss of whole-body lean mass, thereby worsening the systemic presentation of MASLD-associated pathological features.

title: Diagnostic variability of mental disorders in adolescence: A longitudinal study across transition boundary age.
abstract: Correct psychiatric diagnoses represent a prerequisite for the efficacy of treatment, especially during adolescence, a critical period for the onset of mental health disorders. Diagnoses can evolve over time, influenced by factors such as changes in symptoms, treatment effects, and comorbidities. The transition from Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) to Adult Mental Health Services (AMHS) presents challenges due to differences in diagnostic criteria and treatment approaches. This study explores whether and how psychiatric diagnoses change during this transition, aiming to examine the prevalence and composition of primary diagnoses and identify predictors of diagnostic change. From the MILESTONE project total sample, 770 participants aged 17-19 with available diagnoses and clinical data were included and assessed at four-time points. We categorised participants into 10 diagnostic groups based on shared clinical features. Statistical analysis included multilevel logistic regression to examine diagnosis changes, with a Sankey plot to visualise transitions. Clinically, anxiety/trauma disorders (25.1%) were the most common at baseline, followed by depression/bipolar (21.3%) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (15.6%). Most diagnoses remained stable over time, with showing high stability; depression/bipolar showed moderate stability (80.7%), while schizophrenia spectrum disorders and substance use disorders exhibited nearly perfect consistency (100% and 85.7%, respectively). Multilevel logistic regression revealed that higher externalising scores (OR = 2.90; p = 0.045) was a predictor of diagnostic change, while being assessed by a psychiatrist (p = 0.037) was an index of diagnostic stability over time. This study highlights the diagnostic stability of most psychiatric conditions during the transition from CAMHS to AMHS. Given the complexity of adolescent mental health, accurate and continuous assessment is crucial. Understanding the evolving nature of psychiatric symptoms during adolescence will improve diagnostic accuracy and inform better interventions, fostering long-term mental health outcomes.

title: Patient-specific functional networks track early cognitive alterations and minor hallucinations in Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Minor hallucinations (MHs) affect up to 40% of patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) and are early indicators of cognitive decline. Unlike previous group-level studies, connectome-based brain fingerprinting enables the capture of individualized neural features. Leveraging this framework in a cross-sectional cohort of patients with Parkinson's disease with and without MHs using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging, here we show that each patient exhibits a unique brain fingerprint, irrespective of MH status. The most individualized features were associated with clinically relevant measures such as motor-symptom severity and cognitive performance. Patients with MHs showed a loss of individual-specific features in brain networks linked to cognitive health, whereas the cerebellar-to-cortex connectivity-typically less distinctive-became more prominent, emphasizing the role of somatosensory and motor integration in MH pathogenesis. Moreover, MH-related fingerprint regions mapped onto cortical territories with lower densities of neurotransmitter systems implicated in hallucinations. Overall, our fully data-driven findings reveal a distinct, patient-specific signature that differentiates patients with Parkinson's disease and MHs.

title: Applications of OptoProfilin in Living Cells for the Imaging of Focal Adhesions and Stress-Associated Phenotypes.
abstract: Cellular stress induces profound changes in cytoskeletal organization and biomolecular condensate formation. Traditional approaches for monitoring cellular stress often require multi-component biosensors, endpoint staining procedures, or indirect biochemical measurements. Here, we describe a protocol for the use of OptoProfilin, a genetically encoded single-component optogenetic biosensor derived from Profilin-1 fused to Cryptochrome 2 (Cry2) and mCherry. Following transient expression in mammalian cells, OptoProfilin exhibits light-dependent localization to focal adhesions under non-stressed conditions and transitions to punctate condensates under energetic, oxidative, osmotic, and senescence-associated stress conditions. The protocol includes transient transfection, induction of cellular stress, live-cell imaging, immunofluorescence validation, and quantitative image analysis. While this protocol describes imaging on a Leica widefield fluorescence microscope, it can readily be extended to other microscopy platforms. As a stand-alone biosensor that produces visually distinct responses in stressed versus non-stressed cells, OptoProfilin provides a convenient platform for investigating stress-associated cytoskeletal remodeling and biomolecular condensate formation. Key features • Single-component optogenetic biosensor for monitoring cellular stress. • Distinguishes stressed and unstressed cells through distinct localization phenotypes. • Compatible with live-cell imaging, fixed-cell analysis, and immunofluorescence. • Applicable to energetic, oxidative, osmotic, and senescence-associated stress models.

title: Structured missingness in biomedical research.
abstract: Missing data are ubiquitous in biomedical research, and become particularly problematic when combining data from multiple clinical studies, an increasingly common practice for building models that generalise across populations. This process introduces complex structured patterns of missing data ('structured missingness'), where one study may omit variables that another collects, leaving deterministic gaps that standard imputation methods were not designed to handle. Here, we show that many popular imputation algorithms systematically fail under structured missingness, distorting the underlying statistical properties of the data in ways that conventional accuracy metrics cannot detect. Methods designed to preserve data distributions are more robust, and a hierarchical modelling approach that explicitly accounts for site-specific differences further improves performance. We introduce a multi-metric evaluation framework and a practical decision guide to support method selection. Our findings highlight the need for more principled imputation approaches in multi-site biomedical research and provide concrete tools to address this challenge.

title: Gut microbiota and the gut-brain axis in autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: A scoping review of shared and disorder-specific mechanistic pathways.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are among the most prevalent neurodevelopmental conditions worldwide, yet the biological mechanisms driving their onset and phenotypic variability remain incompletely understood. The gut-brain axis (GBA), a bidirectional network linking intestinal microbial communities to central nervous system function through endocrine, immune, neural, and metabolic pathways, has emerged as a candidate mechanism through which environmental factors interact with genetic susceptibility to shape neurodevelopmental outcomes. To systematically map the peer-reviewed evidence on gut microbiome-related mechanistic pathways in ASD and ADHD, we delineated features common to both disorders and identified areas of divergence and knowledge gaps requiring further investigation. A scoping review was performed following the PRISMA Extension for the Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) framework. PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for peer-reviewed studies published January 2018 through March 2025. Studies addressing gut microbiome composition, GBA signaling, or microbiome-directed interventions in ASD or ADHD were eligible for inclusion. Extracted data were synthesized using inductive thematic analysis via Covidence software. Forty-five studies satisfied the eligibility criteria. Inductive analysis produced five mechanistic themes: Endocrine dysregulation and microbial metabolite signaling; neuronal signaling and neurotransmitter modulation; immune activation and neuroinflammation; gene-microbiota-environment interactions; and microbiota-targeted interventions. Studies on both disorders demonstrated modifications involving taxa with short-chain-fatty-acid-producing capacity; however, findings were varied and did not prove a common reduction in butyrate production. ASD was marked by pronounced dysregulation of the serotonergic system and tryptophan-kynurenine pathway and increased hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis responsiveness. On the other hand, the results in ADHD were majorly cross-sectional or preliminary, and the widely-m recognized dopaminergic dysfunction in ADHD has not been associated to specific microbiota alterations to date. Evidence demonstrates the GBA as a useful research conceptual for investigating ASD and ADHD, although the strength of mechanistic evidence differs substantially between the two disorders. Translating these insights into therapeutic strategies will require longitudinal, multi-omic research designs capable of establishing causality and enabling patient stratification for precision microbiome-based interventions.

title: Nanoparticles in the Diagnosis and Management of Stroke: A Review.
abstract: Stroke is the third leading cause of death and the fourth leading cause of disability-adjusted life years worldwide, yet disease-modifying treatment remains largely confined to reperfusion of large-vessel ischemic occlusion within a narrow window. No neuroprotective or hemostatic agent has entered routine practice. Engineered nanoparticles have been proposed to improve delivery across the blood-brain barrier, concentrate drug within the ischemic or perihematomal microenvironment, and add imaging or sensing functions. The resulting literature is large but fragmented across platforms, models, and outcome measures, so it is not evident which platforms carry the strongest evidence or which are closest to clinical evaluation. This narrative review synthesizes preclinical and clinical evidence on nanoparticle-based diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, and monitoring in ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception to July 2025 using predefined Boolean strings and assigned each included study an evidence tier to separate extrapolated and cross-field evidence from stroke-specific data. Comparative tables summarize nanoparticle type, payload, model, route, dose, treatment window, particle size and surface charge, principal outcomes, safety assessment, and translational readiness. Therapeutic evidence is almost entirely preclinical: Efficacy has been shown in young, male, comorbidity-free rodents treated within minutes of reperfusion and followed for 24 h to 28 days, with group sizes typically between three and 15, and few studies reporting any bleeding or coagulation endpoint. Diagnostic applications are closer to patients because iron-oxide nanoparticles have already been given to humans, although not for imaging. We identified seven registered clinical studies of nanoparticle-related interventions in stroke; one perfluorocarbon nanodroplet emulsion completed a randomized dose-escalation trial in acute ischemic stroke, the EU Clinical Trials Register returned none, and none exists in hemorrhagic stroke. Nanoparticle platforms, therefore, remain investigational, and progress will depend less on new chemistry than on comorbid and large-animal models, realistic treatment windows, systematic reporting of bleeding risk and of interference with follow-up imaging, and reproducible manufacturing.

title: Aluminium as a Metalloestrogen: Toxicological Pathways, Endocrine Disruption and Systemic Health Implications.
abstract: Aluminium (Al) is the most abundant metal in the Earth's crust and a common environmental contaminant due to industrial processes, recycling and consumer goods. Aluminium can enter the human body via the gastrointestinal, respiratory, and skin routes, as well as through injection, although this is not essential for biological function. It can then accumulate in different organs. Its physicochemical properties enable it to displace vital metals, bind to biomolecules and interfere with cellular processes, leading to genotoxicity, oxidative stress and protein misfolding. Aluminium toxicity impacts various body systems, such as neurodegeneration, bone disorders, heart conditions, endocrine disruption and reproductive issues. Notably, Al acts as a metalloestrogen, mimicking or disrupting estrogen receptor signaling. This interference affects the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and changes estrogen-dependent processes in both males and females. This review explores Al's systemic toxicology and its emerging function as an endocrine disruptor, highlighting its dual nature as both a sustainable industrial resource and a common biological toxin. The findings highlight important public health issues and suggest the need for further research into how Al interacts with estrogen receptors to improve prevention and treatment.

title: Orthoptek Magnocellular Stimulation for Amblyopia Across Age Groups: Visual Recovery Beyond Childhood.
abstract: To assess the outcome of Orthoptek Magnocellular Stimulator (OMS) therapy on visual acuity, binocular vision and stereopsis in patients with amblyopia across various age groups and to evaluate treatment efficacy. This prospective observational study included 106 patients with amblyopia who received OMS therapy. A 20-session course (30 minutes per session) was prescribed; actual treatment exposure varied and averaged 5.17 sessions. We assessed outcomes at the last available post-treatment visit (mean follow-up, 36.79 days; median, one day). We compared pre- and post-treatment visual acuity, stereopsis, central macular thickness (CMT) and retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) thickness. We performed regression analyses to identify factors associated with the final visual outcome. Study participants' mean age was 17.55 ± 13.91 years. Refractive amblyopia was the most common subtype (67.9%), followed by strabismic amblyopia (30.2%). Mean amblyopic-eye visual acuity improved from 0.97 ± 0.53 to 0.75 ± 0.52 logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution (logMAR) (p < 0.001). Distance stereopsis improved significantly from 349.24 ± 281.62 to 291.05 ± 271.96 arc seconds (p < 0.001), while near stereopsis remained unchanged (p = 0.261). Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed no clinically meaningful change in RNFL thickness. A small increase in amblyopic-eye CMT was statistically significant (mean change, 6.87 µm; p = 0.013) but was not associated with visual improvement and was considered of uncertain clinical relevance. Baseline visual acuity was the strongest predictor of outcome (β = 0.82, p < 0.001). Greater treatment exposure was independently associated with better visual recovery (β = -0.021, p = 0.014), whereas age, follow-up duration and amblyopia subtype were not significant predictors. Orthoptek Magnocellular Stimulator therapy was associated with improved visual acuity and distance stereopsis. Retinal nerve fibre layer thickness remained stable, while the small statistically significant increase in amblyopic-eye CMT was not associated with visual improvement and had uncertain clinical significance. The absence of an age-related association suggests that visual improvement may be achievable beyond the traditional critical period. These preliminary findings support further controlled evaluation of OMS as a potential adjunct to amblyopia rehabilitation in younger and older patients.

title: Adverse effects of vaping on human health: a brief review of mechanisms and long-term consequences.
journal: Arhiv za higijenu rada i toksikologiju
abstract: Vaping, often advertised as a safe alternative to traditional tobacco smoking, has recently been subjected to active scientific research due to its potential adverse effects on human health. This narrative review synthesises selected recent literature to provide a comprehensive view of the systemic risks associated with the use of electronic cigarettes. It lists key chemical components (propylene glycol, vegetable glycerine, nicotine, and flavourings) and thermal decomposition products of vape aerosol (formaldehyde, acrolein, propylene oxide, glycidol) and evaluates their multi-systemic toxic effects and clinical manifestations, as well as specific effects on the respiratory, cardiovascular, immune, and nervous systems. Current data suggest that vaping can lead to a wide range of acute and chronic diseases, including the e-cigarette or vaping-associated lung injury (EVALI) and obliterative bronchiolitis and increase the risk of developing oncological, cardiovascular, and neurological diseases. Particularly sensitive is the developing adolescent brain. A growing body of evidence indicates that vaping is not "less harmful" but merely "differently" harmful and calls for further long-term research and strengthened public health regulation.

title: Selenium-Enriched Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus Alleviates Hypobaric Hypoxia-Induced Brain Injury via Regulation of Gut Microbiota and Neurotransmitter Homeostasis.
abstract: Brain injury induced by hypobaric hypoxia is a concern for individuals exposed to high-altitude environments. This study evaluated the protective potential of prophylactic selenium-enriched Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus (SeLRS) administration in C57BL/6 mice exposed to hypobaric hypoxia. Results showed that just 1 day of hypoxic exposure induced significant anxiety-like, depressive-like, and cognitive impairments, accompanied by hippocampal-amygdala structural damage, a decreased glutamate/gamma-aminobutyric acid ratio, and elevated oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. Critically, injury related abnormalities were still evident after 7 days of exposure, indicating that hypobaric hypoxia-associated brain injury was sustained under prolonged exposure conditions. Oral administration of SeLRS significantly improved behavioral and cognitive deficits, reduced neuroinflammation, attenuated hippocampal-amygdala damage. SeLRS administration was also associated with altered whole-brain glutamate content and amelioration of gut microbiota dysbiosis. 16S rRNA sequencing showed changes in the relative abundances of several taxa, including Muribaculum, Clostridium, Prevotella, and Akkermansia, which have previously been linked to neurotransmitter-related metabolic pathways. Overall, these findings support the potential of the complete SeLRS preparation as a probiotic-based nutritional strategy for mitigating hypobaric hypoxia-associated brain injury.

title: Beyond energy balance: 2-arachidonoylglycerol at the crossroads of obesity, inflammation, and metabolic dysfunction.
abstract: Obesity is the rising public health concern of every household to globally which can now be characterized as a pandemic. The growing prevalence of obesity draws researcher's attention for a deeper understanding of its pathologies and available therapeutic strategies. The known pathologies of the obesity only turns around chronic energy imbalance between consumed calories and calories burnt. There is need to understand intricate relationship between Gut Brain Adipose axis and the complex pathophysiology of obesity which remains incompletely understood. Thus, before a cure, we need to understand the pathology of obesity in a deeper way. Emerging evidences suggest the endocannabinoid system (ECS) as an underappreciated mediator of obesity pathogenesis. In particular, the endocannabinoid 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG) levels are elevated in obesity, acting as a key signaling hub. 2-AG integrates central and peripheral pathways that govern appetite, reward-driven feeding, energy balance, adipogenesis, insulin signaling, mitochondrial function, and immune activation. This review is focussed on 2-AG as a mechanistic intersection at neuroendocrine control of energy balance with metabolic, mitochondrial, oxidative, and inflammatory processes, while critically distinguishing direct evidence for 2-AG, therapeutic gaps, and future perspectives of targeting cannabinoid pharmacology. Importantly, this review discusses that how 2-AG signaling may intersects with insulin/PI3K/AKT, AMPK, PPARs, and NF-κB pathways, amplifying metabolic dysfunction and obesity. This review provides insights on how 2-AG may target different obesity pathogenesis and may pave the way for development of newer targeted interventions. We highlight 2-AG's multi-organ signaling crosstalk and discuss how modulating the 2-AG/ECS axis may yield novel therapeutic strategies for obesity.

title: The Gut-Brain Axis and Neurodegenerative Diseases: From Mechanistic Pathways to Therapeutic Interventions.
abstract: As the global population ages, the incidence of neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs) has increased. Neurodegenerative diseases have complex pathogenesis and currently lack fundamental treatment methods. The gut-brain axis (GBA) participates in the pathogenesis of NDDs through bidirectional communication between the gut microbiota and the central nervous system (CNS). This review systematically introduces the pathogenic characteristics of representative NDDs such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and multiple sclerosis (MS), as well as the association mechanisms between these diseases and GBA. The pathogenic characteristics of NDDs are closely related to changes in the composition of the gut microbiota and differences in gut microbiota metabolites (such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), neurotransmitters, tryptophan metabolites, etc.). These changes influence the CNS through multiple pathways, including neuroendocrine, vagus nerve, and immune regulation, ultimately contributing to the onset and progression of the diseases. Furthermore, we have collected and summarized preclinical and clinical evidence from recent years regarding therapeutic interventions based on the GBA mechanism, including probiotics, prebiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). Nevertheless, major knowledge gaps remain, particularly regarding causality between gut microbiota changes and NDDs, the underlying molecular mechanisms, and the clinical efficacy of GBA-targeted therapies. This article aims to review the mechanisms of the interaction between the gut microbiota and the brain in neurodegenerative diseases, and based on the existing experimental evidence, provide theoretical basis and future development directions for future prevention and treatment strategies targeting GBA.

title: Chronic Headache: The Interplay of Muscle Tension, its Discrimination, and Body Awareness.
abstract: Chronic pain patients often exhibit altered processing of internal bodily sensations, especially in the musculoskeletal domain, and impaired body awareness. This case-control study investigated the association between resting electromyographic (EMG) activity, musculoskeletal tension discrimination and body awareness in chronic headache (CH) patients compared to healthy controls (HC). Twenty-one patients diagnosed with chronic headache and 22 matched healthy controls performed a muscle tension discrimination task while EMG was recorded from the frontalis (pain-related) and biceps brachii (pain-unrelated) muscles. Questionnaires assessed body awareness and pain-related cognitive and affective factors. Compared to HC, CH patients showed higher resting muscle activity (β = 1.32; p < 0.001) and lower discrimination (β = -0.12; p = 0.007) only in the pain site. CH patients exhibited reduced body awareness (η²p = 0.19; p = 0.003), higher anxiety (β = 3.10; p = 0.032), catastrophizing (η²p = 0.30; p < 0.001), and helplessness (η²p = 0.19; p = 0.004). Notably, lower muscle tension discrimination was associated with both higher resting frontalis EMG (ρs = -0.31; p = 0.043) and catastrophizing (ρs = -0.39; p = 0.009). Patients with CH exhibit a site-specific deficit in muscle tension discrimination, accompanied by elevated resting pericranial muscle tension, reduced body awareness, and maladaptive cognitive coping strategies. The association between catastrophizing and impaired discrimination highlights the interplay between cognitive-affective factors and psychophysiological dysregulation in CH. These findings underscore the importance of multidimensional assessment in patients with CH in order to identify targeted psychophysiological treatment.

title: EEG Microstates are Not Associated with Psychotic Symptoms, Neurocognitive Domains or Psychosocial Functioning in Adolescents and Young Adults with Clinical High Risk for Psychosis.
abstract: EEG microstates are brief and discrete topographic patterns of electrical brain activity. Microstates last for 60-120 milliseconds, are thought to represent transient, quasi-stable neural networks, and traditionally four distinct classes (A-D) are distinguished. One of the core concepts of present neuroscience is that neuroimaging is able to capture meaningful networks of brain activity, which can be translated into specific cognitive functions. Following this idea, each microstate might correspond to specific core brain functions. Importantly, these cognitive functions are impaired in mental disorders. Clinical high-risk (CHR) refers to a state associated with an increased risk of developing psychosis. Previous research has demonstrated consistent microstate alterations in CHR individuals (especially in class D), as well as in psychosis. However, the neurobiological and functional meaning of microstate alterations in CHR populations is still elusive. Since the CHR state is associated with reduced neurocognition (e.g., processing speed, verbal memory, executive functions) in combination with specific clinical symptoms and impairments in psychosocial functioning, relationships between resting-state microstates and these domains were examined in a large cross-sectional cohort of CHR individuals (n = 100). Contrary to our expectations, no significant correlations were found for these clinical measures. The finding suggests that while microstate parameters may differ between CHR individuals and controls, these alterations do not seem to directly reflect the neurobiology of clinical symptoms or neurocognitive and psychosocial functions. EEG microstate deviations as candidate trait biomarker therefore require further investigation and validation in longitudinal studies to establish their stability and predictive value.

title: Characterizing hippocampal activation during pattern separation with multi-echo fMRI in cognitively normal older adults.
abstract: Hippocampal hyperactivity, detected with mnemonic similarity task (MST) fMRI, is both a promising marker of risk and a probable driver of degeneration in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, implementation of such fMRI in interventional research is limited by long scan times and the absence of a framework for identifying prospective participants with hyperactivity who could be targeted with therapeutic approaches aimed at reducing this activity. We used multi-echo fMRI during the MST, an episodic memory task previously shown to engage hippocampal subfields CA3 and dentate gyrus (DG), to characterize activity profiles in 33 cognitively normal older adults. We compared MST-related CA3 and DG activation and behavioural performance across subsets of eight task runs. Behavioural and activation effects were equivalent for the first set of four runs (Runs-A) and the second set (Runs-B), suggesting that robust data can be obtained with four runs. Left and right CA3 + DG activation did not differ. We provide an exemplar framework for the derivation of a threshold for single-participant classification of elevated hippocampal activation as an indicator of AD risk in cognitively normal older individuals. Scalable (~22 min) multi-echo MST fMRI robustly captures hippocampal activation and provides a framework for individual-level characterization of hippocampal function in cognitively normal older adults. This enables individualized detection of elevated hippocampal activation as a modifiable risk factor and may guide enrolment into prevention trials targeting preclinical AD.

title: Frontal cortical neuroinflammation and circulating biomarkers following cardiopulmonary bypass in sheep.
abstract: Cerebral hypoxia and neuroinflammation have been implicated in neurocognitive disorders following cardiac surgery, but their postoperative trajectory and relationship with circulating biomarkers are poorly defined. We investigated cerebral tissue oxygenation, neuroinflammation, and plasma biomarkers of neurodegeneration over 4 weeks after cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) in sheep. Sixteen adult Merino ewes underwent CPB with a 2-h aortic cross-clamp and recovered for either 48 h (n = 8) or 4 weeks (n = 8). Cerebral tissue oxygenation was monitored. Neuroinflammation was quantified by morphometric analyses of microglia and astrocytes in the frontal cortex in both CPB groups and a naïve control group (n = 8). Plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) were measured serially. Compared with pre-CPB baseline, cerebral tissue oxygenation did not change significantly in the 48-h or 4-week period. In the 48-h post-CPB group, microglial soma sphericity was reduced (0.79 ± 0.04 vs. 0.83 ± 0.02, P = 0.018) compared with naïve controls, indicating microglial activation. Astrocytic GFAP-positive area was also elevated (17 ± 2% vs. 10 ± 2%, P = 0.026). In the 4-week post-CPB group, these measures did not differ significantly from naïve controls. Plasma NfL rose from 138 [96-185] pg/mL at baseline to 198 [149-265] pg/mL at 48 h (P = 0.0007), while GFAP peaked at the end of CPB (14.4 [4.7-32.4] vs. 3.0 [1.3-4.5] pg/mL, P < 0.0001) and normalised by 48 h. CPB induced neuroinflammation characterised by frontal cortical microglial activation and astrogliosis, accompanied by temporal elevations in plasma GFAP and NfL.
