title: Caregiver Burden and Its Determinants After Subthalamic Nucleus Deep Brain Stimulation for Parkinson's Disease: A Cross-Sectional Long-Term Follow-Up Study.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, leading to increasing functional dependence even after deep brain stimulation (DBS). Although DBS improves motor outcomes, its long-term impact on caregiver burden remains poorly understood. Our aims were to evaluate caregiver burden after subthalamic nucleus (STN)-DBS and identify patient- and caregiver-related factors associated with burden across different postoperative time points. A cross-sectional study of caregivers of PD patients who underwent STN-DBS at a tertiary center, stratified by time since surgery (2-3, 5-6, 10-11, and ≥15 years), was conducted. Caregivers completed the Zarit Burden Interview, Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, and an investigator-developed questionnaire. Patient clinical data, including the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS), Part III, scores, were obtained from medical records. Group comparisons and multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with caregiver burden. Eighty-eight patient-caregiver pairs were included. Caregivers were predominantly female (62.5%), with a mean age of 60.0 ± 12.3 years. Caregiver burden was mild to moderate but increased independently with longer time postsurgery. Higher burden was associated with younger caregiver age, higher anxiety and depression scores, greater caregiving time, less personal time, and patient-related factors, including dysphagia, dementia, and male sex. Motor severity (UPDRS III, falls, postural instability) was not associated with caregiver burden. Most caregivers considered STN-DBS beneficial and would choose surgery again. Caregiver burden increased with longer time after STN-DBS and was associated with dementia, dysphagia, and caregiver-related factors but not with motor severity. Several associated factors are potentially modifiable, supporting systematic caregiver assessment and targeted interventions as part of long-term PD management.

title: Disease Duration Differentiates Freezing of Gait Response to Subthalamic and Nigral Stimulation for Parkinson's Disease in an Exploratory Multicenter Controlled Trial.
abstract: Freezing of gait (FoG) belongs to most pressing unmet symptoms in the treatment of Parkinson's disease. To explore whether combined subthalamic and nigral (STN + SNr) deep brain stimulation improves FoG compared with optimized STN stimulation alone; to identify clinical variables associated with therapeutic response. In this exploratory multicenter randomized controlled double-blind trial, we recruited patients from our existing cohorts and randomized them 1:1 to STN or STN + SNr. After baseline, patients were followed with close interim visits (visits 1-5) for 90 days (visit 6). The Freezing of Gait Assessment Course (FoG-AC) was the primary endpoint and was evaluated at P < 0.2 with exploratory intent. Secondary endpoints assessed responder rates, treatment dynamics, predictors of response, and patient preferences. At V6, STN (n = 23) and STN + SNr (n = 22) FoG-AC outcomes did not differ significantly. We identified responders with clinically meaningful FoG improvement in both the STN (n = 7) and STN + SNr (n = 8) groups. In STN + SNr responders, mean disease duration was ~12 years, which was ~4.5 years shorter than in non-responders, but there were no differences in motor and cognitive functions. Treatment dynamics suggested that FoG responders improved slowly and gradually. The STN + SNr responder group showed numerically stronger FoG improvement compared with STN responders. Additionally, 15 STN compared to 10 STN + SNr patients wished to change treatment after the RCT phase and before unblinding. Both STN and STN + SNr treatment was safe. Future trials evaluating adjunctive STN + SNr stimulation should stratify patients by disease duration to optimize outcomes.

title: Metabolomics Based Biomarkers of Green Beans Intake.
abstract: While there is considerable interest in legumes as a food source, there are no validated biomarkers for green beans (Phaseolus vulgaris, L.) intake. The objective of the current work is to identify and assess the dose-response of food intake biomarkers of green beans. In an acute intervention study, 27 participants consumed green beans in the study center and urine samples were collected pre- and post-consumption. Metabolites were measured by nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR) and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). Statistical analysis determined features that changed post-consumption of green beans. Selected metabolites were assessed for dose-response in a follow-up study (n = 16). Analysis revealed 745 1H-NMR spectral regions and 318 LC-MS features that increased in intensity over time following consumption of green beans. Three 1H-NMR and 12 LC-MS metabolites displayed a dose-response relationship to increasing portion size of green beans (p <0.05), including amino acid conjugates (glycine conjugate, N-phenylacetylglutamine), hydroxyabscisic acid glucuronide and amino-hydroxybenzoic acid. Partial least squares discriminant analysis predicted low or high green bean intake with 91.6% accuracy. We identified 15 urinary food intake biomarkers of green beans. A biomarker panel classified individuals as low or high green bean consumers with good accuracy, progressing ongoing efforts to improve dietary assessment methods.

title: Green Extraction of Phenolic Compounds From Pistacia lentiscus Leaves Coupled With LC-MS Characterization and Structure-Based Enzyme Inhibition Analysis.
abstract: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and urease are critical enzymes involved in various pathological conditions associated with cellular and tissue damage. Natural products are increasingly explored as safer alternatives to synthetic inhibitors. This study evaluates the phytochemical composition and enzyme inhibitory potential of Pistacia lentiscus leaves using a green extraction approach. Bioactive compounds were extracted via lactic acid-assisted ultrasound, and the crude extract was characterized for total phenolics, flavonoids, LC-MS profile, and in vitro inhibition of acetylcholinesterase and urease. Molecular docking was performed to investigate ligand-enzyme interactions. The extract contained 142.13 ± 0.06 mg GAE/g DW of polyphenols and 16.17 ± 0.02 mg QE/g DW of flavonoids. LC-MS analysis identified phenolic acids, phenolic glycosides, coumarins, and multiple flavonoid subclasses, including flavonols, flavanols, flavanones, flavones, and flavonolignans. The extract exhibited significant inhibition of both enzymes. Docking studies revealed key interactions, such as hydrogen bonds, π-alkyl, and π-sigma, within the active sites, with hesperidin and verbascoside showing the strongest binding affinities (acetylcholinesterase: -10.1 and -10.2 kcal/mol; urease: -9.6 and -9.2 kcal/mol, respectively). These results demonstrate that ultrasound-assisted lactic acid extraction efficiently isolates phenolic compounds from P. lentiscus, and the identified metabolites may serve as promising templates for the development of potent enzyme inhibitors.

title: In Vitro Antioxidant, Antibacterial, and Cholinesterase-Inhibitory Properties of an Aqueous Euphorbia macroclada Root Extract Obtained by Ultrasound-Assisted Extraction.
abstract: In the present study, the aqueous extract obtained from the roots of Euphorbia macroclada via ultrasound-assisted extraction (Ult-ER) was evaluated for its anticholinesterase (AChE and BChE), antioxidant, and antibacterial activities. While the extract exhibited weak inhibition against AChE (IC50: 507.69 ± 17.95 mg/mL), it showed relatively greater inhibitory activity against BChE (IC50: 22.41 ± 0.49 mg/mL). In antioxidant assays, Ult-ER exhibited measurable antioxidant responses, with DPPH and ABTS+ radical-scavenging capacities of 18.33 ± 0.49 and 119.59 ± 1.86 mg TE/L, respectively. Its Fe3 + and Cu2 + reducing capacities were 128.51 ± 12.57 and 670.33 ± 11.59 mg TE/L, respectively. The total phenolic and flavonoid contents were 84.80 ± 3.31 mg GAE/g and 60.67 ± 2.29 mg QE/g, while the total antioxidant capacity was 9.78 ± 0.44 mg TE/g and 15.62 ± 1.85 mg BHAE/g. In the antibacterial evaluation, Ult-ER at the highest tested concentration of 8 mg/mL exhibited inhibitory activity against all tested strains, including Enterococcus faecalis ATCC 29212, Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923, Escherichia coli ATCC 25922, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa ATCC 27853, whereas no detectable inhibition was observed at lower concentrations.

title: Evaluation of the brachial plexus and spinal cord with diffusion tensor imaging and synthetic MRI in obstetric brachial plexus palsy: DTI of brachial plexus and spinal cord in OBPP.
abstract: Obstetric brachial plexus palsy (OBPP) is conventionally staged as a peripheral nerve injury, yet conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) poorly reflects microstructural neural and spinal cord changes. We evaluate whether magnetic resonance image compilation (MAGIC), a form of synthetic MRI, shows strong agreement with conventional T2-weighted short-tau inversion recovery (T2-STIR) for postganglionic injury detection, compare diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics between injured and adjacent intact segments of the brachial plexus and spinal cord, and explore whether these metrics predict recovery at 2-year follow-up in infants with OBPP. In this single-center cohort with prospective enrollment and ambispective outcome assessment, 40 infants (aged 3-30 weeks) with unilateral OBPP underwent 3-T MRI during physiological sleep, comprising conventional T2-STIR, synthetic MRI (MAGIC T2-STIR), and DTI. Two blinded neuroradiologists compared synthetic and conventional sequences for postganglionic lesion detection (weighted κ). The DTI-derived fractional anisotropy (FA) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) were measured at the neural foramen (dorsal root ganglion level) and spinal cord at every injured segment and at the nearest intact segments above and below; per infant, the minimum injured value and the mean intact value were compared and related to Narakas type and 2-year recovery. Synthetic MRI showed strong agreement with conventional T2-STIR (κ = 0.84-1.00); the intraobserver repeatability of DTI measurements was good to excellent [intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) = 0.842-0.999), except for intact spinal cord ADC (ICC = 0.662). Compared with intact reference segments, injured segments showed lower FA and higher ADC at both the neural foramen (FA = 0.236 ± 0.092 vs. 0.433 ± 0.130; ADC = 2,116 ×10-6 vs. 1,191.25 ×10-6 mm2/s) and the spinal cord (FA = 0.321 ± 0.107 vs. 0.448 ± 0.143; ADC = 2,253.5 ×10-6 vs. 1,191 ×10-6 mm2/s) (all P < 0.001). Neither FA nor ADC differed by Narakas type or predicted 2-year recovery. Synthetic MRI showed strong agreement with conventional T2-STIR for the detection of postganglionic OBPP and provided six contrasts from a single acquisition of similar duration; DTI abnormalities at injured segments extended to the spinal cord, suggesting that microstructural change in OBPP may not be confined to the peripheral nerve. Segmental DTI abnormality within the spinal cord raises the possibility that OBPP injury extends centrally; confirmation would require higher-resolution acquisition, technical validation against partial-volume and cerebrospinal fluid effects, and larger longitudinal cohorts before any implication for injury classification.

title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlations in THAP1-Associated Dystonia: A Multicentric Observational Study.
abstract: DYT-THAP1 is a recognized cause of early-onset isolated dystonia. However, available data are largely derived from European cohorts, limiting understanding of genetic diversity, phenotype variability, and treatment response in underrepresented populations. To characterize the clinical spectrum, genetic architecture, genotype-phenotype correlations, and treatment outcomes in Asian Indian patients with DYT-THAP1. This multicentric, cross-sectional study included patients harboring pathogenic or likely pathogenic THAP1 variants. Clinical features, neuroimaging, and treatment responses were systematically assessed. Genetic testing comprised whole-exome sequencing, clinical exome sequencing, targeted gene panels, or Sanger sequencing. Variants were classified using ACMG criteria, and genotype-phenotype associations were analyzed. Twenty-six patients from 22 families were identified (17 males; mean age 29.4 ± 12.9 years). Median age at onset was 13.0 years (IQR 10.0-23.5), with 69.2% presenting before 20 years. Dystonia commonly involved the upper limbs (68%), cervical region (28%), and larynx (20%) at onset, with progression to generalized dystonia in 64%. Seventeen distinct heterozygous THAP1 variants were detected, of which 10 (58.8%) were novel. Loss-of-function variants affected 57.7% of patients and were associated with greater motor severity (P = 0.023) and more frequent positive family history (P = 0.019). Exon 2 variants were more frequent in patients with tremor (P = 0.045). This study highlights the evolving mutational landscape of DYT-THAP1 beyond variants reported in Caucasian pedigrees and demonstrates novel, clinically relevant genotype-phenotype associations, underscoring the value of including underrepresented populations to bridge knowledge gaps in rare diseases.

title: Methylphenidate and Long-Term Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
abstract: Cardiovascular safety of methylphenidate remains a matter of debate. To evaluate the long-term cardiovascular risk associated with methylphenidate use, a cohort study was conducted using the French National Health Data System. New users were defined by a first methylphenidate dispensation (index date) between January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2023. Each new user was matched with three nonusers by sex and by month and year of birth. Individuals with prior cardiovascular disease or relevant cardiovascular comorbidities were excluded. The primary outcome was cardiovascular disease, defined by International Classification of Diseases codes or antihypertensive drug use. Cox proportional hazards models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (HRs), accounting for demographic and clinical covariates. Negative control outcomes were used to assess residual confounding, allowing the derivation of calibrated HRs and confidence intervals. A total of 212 216 new users and 636 648 matching nonusers were included. Mean age was 13.7 years and 72% were males. Over a follow-up of ~4 years, 3858 cardiovascular diseases occurred (0.45%): 1960 in new users (9.2 per 1000) and 1898 in nonusers (3 per 1000). The adjusted HR was 2.37 (95% CI [2.21; 2.54]), with a calibrated HR of 1.85 (95% CI [1.55; 2.21]). The results suggest that methylphenidate use may be associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular diseases. Although the calibrated estimates indicate attenuation due to residual confounding, the association remained statistically significant. This supports recommendations for cardiovascular monitoring during treatment.

title: Cervical Dystonia Treatment with Injections Supplemented by Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation: The D-TWIST Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: For some patients with cervical dystonia (CD), botulinum toxin (BoNT) injections last less than 12 weeks. To determine if a novel, accelerated repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) protocol is a safe and feasible adjunctive treatment with BoNT for CD. Patients with CD reporting BoNT benefit lasting ≤9 weeks were enrolled in a randomized double-blind, sham-controlled, crossover study. The Toronto Western Spasmodic Torticollis Rating Scale (TWSTRS), mood, cognitive, and gait measures were collected before, after, and 2-weeks following rTMS/SHAM. In a homogenous subset of patients (N = 4/5), TWSTRS scores were lower 2-weeks following rTMS, but evidence of an effect was potentially limited by sample size. There was little evidence of rTMS effects on mood, cognition, or gait. Accelerated rTMS for CD was safe, feasible, and well-tolerated; larger randomized studies are needed to determine whether accelerated rTMS may be an effective treatment bridge for dystonia symptoms.

title: Advances in Classification of Human Gastric Enteric Neurons.
Making the Diagnosis of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia in Australia.
abstract: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD) is a genetic disorder associated with recurrent infections and irreversible airway damage. No single diagnostic test exists, necessitating use of a diagnostic algorithm that varies internationally. This retrospective study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics of patients, and algorithm used to diagnose PCD in New South Wales between 2014 and 2024. A retrospective review of patients diagnosed with PCD at Concord Repatriation General Hospital (CRGH) from 2014 to 2024 was performed. This study included 52 patients with median age of diagnosis 7.0 years. The diagnostic algorithm consists of nasal nitric oxide (nNO) in patients > 5 years, and nasal brushings for high-speed video microscopy (HSVMA), immunofluorescence (IF) and electron microscopy (EM). Whole exome sequencing is not routine and was performed in 33% of the cohort. The diagnosis was confirmed by a multidisciplinary team that considered the test results and clinical phenotype. Non-diagnostic results occurred in 14% (nNO), 15% (HSVMA), 41% (IF) and 30% (EM) of patients eventually diagnosed with PCD or PCD "highly likely". Cumulatively, 56% of patients had at least one non-diagnostic result. Of the 17 patients who underwent whole exome sequencing with a PCD panel, 41% had diagnostic genetic results. Ciliary studies continue to be the mainstay of PCD diagnosis at CRGH. Although genetic testing is not part of the CRGH diagnostic algorithm, the CRGH algorithm has similar diagnostic performance to the ERS and ATS guidelines.

title: Real-World Use of Avacopan in Antineutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody-Associated Vasculitis: Early and Long-Term Clinical, Renal, and Patient-Reported Outcomes in an Italian Rheumatology-Nephrology Network.
abstract: Complement activation, particularly through the C5a-C5a receptor axis, plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) and may represent an important therapeutic target. Avacopan, an oral C5a receptor antagonist, was the first therapy targeting this pathway to enter in clinical practice. Prospective real-world data on its long-term effectiveness, safety, and impact on quality of life (QoL) remain limited. In the context of an evolving therapeutic and regulatory landscape, such data provide valuable evidence on the clinical effects of C5a receptor inhibition and may inform the development and evaluation of future complement-targeted therapies. The objective of this study was to evaluate the real-world effectiveness, safety, kidney outcomes, and patient-reported outcomes of avacopan in an Italian cohort of patients with granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) or microscopic polyangiitis (MPA). This prospective, multicenter, observational study included patients with newly diagnosed or relapsing GPA or MPA who were started on avacopan therapy across 18 Italian centers. Avacopan was administered in combination with standard immunosuppressive therapy, with or without glucocorticoids (GCs). Clinical remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score = 0), GC-free remission, kidney parameters, laboratory outcomes, adverse events, and patient-reported outcomes assessed by the AAV Patient-Reported Outcome questionnaire were evaluated up to 52 weeks and beyond. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was calculated using the European Kidney Function Consortium equation. Forty-six patients were included (63% women; mean age of 59 years); 61% had relapsing disease, and 70% had kidney involvement at baseline. Clinical remission was achieved by 78%, 88%, and 97% of patients at weeks 12, 26, and 52, respectively. GC-free remission occurred in 20% at week 12 and 55% at week 52. Mean GC dose decreased from 23 mg/day at baseline to 5 mg/day by week 12 (P < 0.001). Kidney function improved over time, with median eGFR increasing from 30.5 mL/min/1.73 m2 at baseline to 53.5 mL/min/1.73 m2 at week 52 (P = 0.002). Significant improvements in QoL were observed as early as week 12 and were sustained until week 52, particularly in the physical function domain. Adverse events were mild to moderate; infections were the most frequent events (40%). Disease relapses were uncommon and occurred exclusively in patients treated for relapsing disease. In this real-world Italian cohort, patients treated with avacopan achieved high remission rates, substantial GC reduction, improvement in kidney function, and sustained QoL benefits. These findings provide prospective real-world evidence on the clinical outcomes associated with C5a receptor inhibition in routine clinical practice while acknowledging the observational design of the study.

title: Psilocybin enhances conditioned place preference learning in planarians.
abstract: Psilocybin has emerged as a promising therapeutic agent, with clinical benefits attributed to enhanced neuroplasticity rather than acute pharmacological effects. However, the fundamental mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. Using planarians as a model system, we investigated whether psilocybin enhances associative learning using a conditioned place preference paradigm. Following a single exposure to 5 µM psilocybin, planarians underwent 5 days of conditioning in which light was paired with sucrose. Psilocybin-treated planarians showed a significantly greater shift in light preference compared to controls (time × group × drug interaction: F(2,38) = 3.3, P < 0.05), with effects persisting at least 6 days post-administration. These findings demonstrate that psilocybin enhances appetitive associative learning in an invertebrate model, supporting the hypothesis that psychedelic-induced neuroplasticity operates through evolutionarily conserved serotonergic mechanisms.

title: A Community's Voice: Community Advisory Boards in ADRD Biomarker Research Among Older Black Women.
journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) disproportionately affect Black/African American (BAA) women, yet this afflicted population remains underrepresented in ADRD biomarker research. As ADRD blood-based biomarkers become increasingly available, research must prioritize equity and inclusivity to determine their diagnostic specificity in minoritized groups. Community Advisory Boards (CABs) are pivotal in ensuring culturally responsive and community-engaged research. This article outlines the formation, operation, and maintenance of the Black Women: Inflammation and Tau Study (BWITS) CAB, which has played a crucial role in guiding the BWITS Research Team by refining research protocols and safeguarding the cultural contexts of the communities it represents. Motivated by a commitment to the BAA community, we advocate for a transformative shift in ADRD research on minoritized populations, emphasizing the need for CAB input to ensure accountability and the implementation of culturally responsive methods, benefiting both the scientific and target communities.

title: Latent profiles of body composition in older adults with hypertension: associations with physical fitness and differences in blood pressure and fasting plasma glucose.
abstract: This study aimed to identify the body composition profiles of older adults with hypertension and examine their associations with physical fitness and cardiometabolic characteristics. This cross-sectional study included 491 community-dwelling older adults with hypertension. Latent profile analysis was conducted using eight body composition indicators. Associations between age, physical fitness components, and profile membership were examined using multinomial logistic regression with a three-step approach. Systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and fasting plasma glucose levels were compared across profiles using one-way analysis of variance. Four profiles were identified: low muscle mass, balanced, high adiposity, and high muscle/low fat ratio. Handgrip strength, balance, and flexibility were significantly associated with profile membership, whereas age and aerobic endurance were not. The high adiposity profile had significantly higher systolic blood pressure than the low muscle and high muscle/low fat profiles, and higher diastolic blood pressure than the low muscle profile. The high muscle/low fat profile was associated with significantly lower fasting plasma glucose levels than the low muscle and high adiposity profiles. Distinct body composition profiles in older adults with hypertension were associated with differences in physical fitness and cardiometabolic characteristics. These findings support the value of a person-centered approach that integrates body composition and physical fitness.

title: Integrative ALS therapy: gene targeted therapy by base editing and potential exercise rehabilitation as synergistic strategies for functional recovery.
abstract: A key pathological hallmark of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is transactive response DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43, encoded by TARDBP) proteinopathy. Mutations in TARDBP and cellular stress can drive nuclear clearance and cytoplasmic aggregation of TDP-43. TDP-43 is an essential nuclear RNA-binding protein that regulates RNA metabolism, and cytoplasmic TDP-43 aggregation leads to aberrant splicing of essential neuronal transcripts including stathmin-2 (STMN2) and unc-13 homolog A (UNC13A). Dysregulated RNA splicing causes cryptic exon (CE) inclusion in STMN2 and UNC13A mRNA, resulting in non-functional proteins and disruption of axonal regeneration and synaptic integrity. Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides and gene-editing platforms can correct STMN2 and UNC13A mis-splicing defects. However, restoring STMN2 and UNC13A expression alone is not sufficient to regenerate neuromuscular junctions or reverse skeletal muscle atrophy, both of which are crucial for functional recovery in patients with ALS. We reviewed gene-targeted treatment strategies and rehabilitative mechanisms that inhibit ALS progression and reverse neuromuscular degeneration by analyzing databases, including Google Scholar, PubMed, and ScienceDirect. We proposed a dual-modality therapeutic approach integrating base-editing-mediated gene therapy with exercise-based rehabilitation. Antisense oligonucleotides and genome editing can restore transcript fidelity by preventing cryptic exons inclusion in STMN2 and UNC13A, thereby stabilizing neuronal function. Gene-targeted therapies halt ALS progression; however, these treatments alone are insufficient to reverse neuromuscular degeneration or achieve functional recovery needed for patients with ALS to return to daily life. Integrated rehabilitation is a crucial step in gene-targeted therapy for ALS. This strategy halts disease progression and restores neuromuscular function, thereby improving the lifespan and quality of life of patients with ALS.

title: Ameliorative Potential of Green and Red Cabbage Extracts Against Teratogenic and Hepatotoxic Effects of Dimenhydrinate in Chick Embryo.
abstract: Dimenhydrinate (DH) is the first generation medicine used as antiemetic. It is neurotoxic in rat and chick embryos. Both green cabbage (GCbg) and red cabbage (RCbg) have many health benefits and red cabbage is also full of anthocyanins and may minimize oxidative stress in chick embryo. The study was designed to check the teratogenic impacts of dimenhydrinate and curative abilities of green and red cabbage extracts against dimenhydrinate in chick embryo through morphometry, histopathology and micrometry. Fertilized eggs were divided into six groups (n = 50): (1) control (Cnt), injected with 0.02 mL distilled water (2) GCbg, injected with 0.02 mL green cabbage extract (3) RCbg, injected with 0.02 mL red cabbage extract (4) DH, injected with 0.02 mL dimenhydrinate (5) DH + GCbg, injected with 0.01 mL dimenhydrinate and 0.01 mL green cabbage extract (6) DH + RCbg, injected with 0.01 mL dimenhydrinate and 0.01 mL red cabbage extract. All groups were administered on the zero day of incubation, and recovery was made on the 14th day. The embryos of DH exposed group indicated significant decrease in embryonic body weight (7.71 ± 2.82 g) and liver weight (0.03 ± 0.02 g) as compared to control group (15.58 ± 0.75 g; 0.35 ± 0.01 g). The prominent morphometric malformations were amelia, phocomelia, microcephaly and microtia. The hepato-histopathologic signs include decreased hepatocytes, irregular hepatocyte cords and sinusoidal space and de-shaping central veins. This study indicated that dimenhydrinate is teratogenic in chick embryo and both cabbages have ability to decrease birth defects and red cabbage indicated more positive potential compared to green cabbage.

title: Myelin Maintenance and Addition Regulate Synaptic Plasticity in the Adult Mouse Cortex.
abstract: Myelin has the capacity to affect synapse number or plasticity across the lifespan. We report that disrupting oligodendrocyte (OL) and myelin maintenance from P57 (Plp-CreERT2:: Myrffl/fl mice) induces myelin loss and impairs action potential conduction and gross motor performance. By studying sparsely labeled layer V pyramidal neurons in the primary motor cortex of P57 + 60 mice, we determined that apical and basal dendritic spine densities were normal; however, more were large, stable mushroom spines that generated larger amplitude miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents. When we instead prevented OL and myelin addition from P57 (Pdgfrα-CreER:: Myrffl/fl mice), action potential conduction velocity, gross motor performance, and spine densities were normal; however, basal dendritic spine morphology was changed. Without adult myelination, the basal dendrites of P57 + 60 mice retained the morphological characteristics of dendrites in P57 + 0 mice, which have a higher proportion of thin, plastic spines. These data indicate that existing myelin imposes limits on the proportion of spines that become mushroom spines, allowing neurons to remain plastic, while adult myelination is required for spine stabilization within the basal but not apical dendritic compartment. These data show that myelin regulates synaptic plasticity within the motor circuit and offer a potential mechanism by which myelination can influence motor skill learning and/or recall.

title: Candidate neurobiological pathways linking physical exercise to cognition in Parkinson's disease: a hypothesis-generating translational framework.
abstract: Cognitive impairment is a major nonmotor symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet effective strategies for preserving cognitive function remain limited. Although physical exercise may confer cognitive benefits, the biological pathways linking exercise to cognition in PD remain incompletely established. This narrative review presents a hypothesis-generating translational framework for 4 candidate mechanistic domains that may contribute to exercise-related cognitive effects in PD. First, exercise-responsive neurotrophic signaling, particularly through brain-derived neurotrophic factor-tropomyosin receptor kinase B, insulin-like growth factor 1, and vascular endothelial growth factor pathways, may support synaptic plasticity, neuronal survival, and neurovascular function. Second, exercise may modulate dopaminergic, cholinergic, and noradrenergic systems and influence corticostriatal plasticity relevant to cognitive function. Third, muscle-derived factors and exercise-induced metabolites may affect neurotrophic signaling, neuronal metabolism, and autophagy-lysosomal clearance of α-synuclein. Fourth, exercise may regulate systemic and central inflammatory responses through cytokine signaling, glial activation, inflammasome pathways, and complement-mediated synaptic remodeling. The evidence supporting these pathways is derived from basic, preclinical, observational, and exercise-intervention studies, but the strength of evidence varies considerably across stages of translation. Direct evidence that exercise-induced biological changes mediate cognitive improvement in patients with PD is lacking. These pathways should therefore be regarded as candidate mechanisms for hypothesis-driven investigation of the cognitive effects of exercise in PD.

title: Targeting the Gut to Modify Parkinson's Disease: From Mechanisms to Potential Therapeutics.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder and its prevalence continues to rise with population aging. Its cardinal motor features arise from the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, accompanied by intraneuronal α-synuclein aggregates known as Lewy bodies. Neuropathological evidence suggests that, in a subset of patients, α-synuclein pathology first appears in the enteric nervous system and ascends to the brain via the gut-brain axis. Consistent with this "body-first" trajectory, a growing body of work has documented distinct alterations in gut microbial composition and microbiota-derived metabolites in people with PD relative to healthy individuals, with some changes detectable in the prodromal phase. Current management, whether dopaminergic pharmacotherapy or deep brain stimulation, alleviates motor symptoms but does not slow neurodegeneration, and long-term treatment is complicated by motor fluctuations and other adverse effects. Therapies directed at the underlying disease process are therefore urgently needed. Because early perturbations of the gut microenvironment appear to contribute to PD pathogenesis, interventions that restore gut homeostasis represent a rational disease-modifying strategy, particularly for patients whose pathology originates in the gut. This review synthesizes current understanding of how the gut microbiota shapes the gut-brain axis in PD, spanning immune, metabolic, neuroendocrine, and neural pathways, and critically appraises the emerging evidence for microbiota-directed interventions, including fecal microbiota transplantation, probiotics, and prebiotics, as candidate disease-modifying therapies.

title: Neurotologic and MRI Correlates of Idiopathic Acute Unilateral Audiovestibulopathy.
abstract: Although MRI can aid in detecting idiopathic acute unilateral audiovestibulopathy (iAUAV), the relationship between imaging and neurotologic findings remains unclear. We retrospectively reviewed the medical records of patients diagnosed with iAUAV at a tertiary hospital in South Korea between March 2018 and September 2025. Neurotologic and imaging data on heavily T2-weighted 3D fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequences were included for analysis. Eighty-four patients with iAUAV were included in the analysis. MRI-positivity was found in 44 patients (52%), with high signal intensities in the vestibule (n = 31), horizontal (HC, n = 27), posterior (PC, n = 24), and anterior canals (AC, n = 22), as well as basal (n = 15), apical (n = 13), and middle turns of the cochlea (n = 10). Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that MRI positivity was negatively associated with vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR) gain for the PC (p = 0.028). The VOR gains for the HC and PC were negatively correlated with the normalized signal intensity ratios of the vestibule (q = 0.021) and each semicircular canal (q = 0.025). 52% of patients with iAUAV showed positivity on precontrast 3D-FLAIR images, showing a strong association with vestibular deficits in the PC. The observed correlation between MRI and neurotologic findings may facilitate the diagnosis and differentiation of iAUAV and provide insight into its underlying pathophysiology as a frequent cause of acute audiovestibulopathy.

title: Preliminary evidence for script generation as an efficient, objective measure of everyday function in older adults.
journal: Journal of clinical and experimental neuropsychology
abstract: Mild difficulties performing everyday activities may emerge early in Alzheimer's disease and Alzheimer's disease-related dementias, creating a need for objective, efficient measures sensitive to subtle functional changes. This study investigated a script generation task (SGT), which required individuals to verbally describe the steps needed to complete familiar everyday activities, as a potential method for detecting mild functional difficulties in older adults with or without mild cognitive impairment (MCI). We examined both human-coded features of script generation and automated linguistic features using natural language processing (NLP). 83 community-dwelling older adults (mean age = 73.59 years; 67% female; 55% White; n = 57 cognitively unimpaired on testing [CU]; n = 26 MCI) completed the SGT, requiring them to describe the steps for four everyday tasks: making toast, preparing instant coffee, making a peanut butter and jelly sandwich, and preparing a lunchbox. SGT performance was scored by human coders for total steps, words, and errors and analyzed using NLP measures of pronoun-to-noun ratio, lexical density, and lexical sophistication. Participants also completed a performance-based test of everyday function (Naturalistic Action Test, NAT), self-report questionnaires regarding everyday function, and cognitive tests. . After controlling for age, education, and estimated IQ, participants with MCI generated significantly fewer SGT steps than CU participants and used more pronouns relative to nouns, reflecting less specificity in their speech. The ability to generate SGT steps was associated with cognitive tests of episodic memory, and both SGT steps and total words were associated with executive function. Participants who generated more SGT words also completed more steps on the NAT. These associations survived correction for multiple comparisons. By contrast, SGT measures were not significantly associated with self-reported everyday functioning after correction for multiple comparisons. Findings provide support for the potential use of the SGT as an objective and efficient measure of mild functional difficulties in older adults. Future work is needed to evaluate the predictive validity of the SGT and to develop automated scoring programs to increase scalability.

title: Schwann Cell-Specific ATG7-Dependent Autophagy Protects Myelin in a Mouse Model of Krabbe Disease.
abstract: Krabbe disease (KD) is a lysosomal storage disorder characterized by severe peripheral demyelination caused by mutations in galactosylceramidase (GALC), leading to the accumulation of galactosylceramide and psychosine. Although psychosine toxicity is central to KD pathology, additional mechanisms likely contribute to myelin dysfunction. Because Schwann cells (SCs) play a critical role in myelin maintenance, and GALC deficiency disrupts lysosomal function, we hypothesized that autophagy is altered in SCs during KD progression. Using a SC-specific Galc conditional knockout (Galc SC cKO) mouse model, we identified early changes in autophagy-related protein levels and increased autophagosome abundance during the pre-symptomatic phase, prior to detectable myelin abnormalities. To assess whether autophagy contributes to disease progression, we selectively deleted Atg7, an essential regulator of canonical autophagy, in SCs. Atg7 deletion alone did not affect myelin or behavior, but its loss in Galc SC cKO mice markedly worsened disease severity. Atg7-Galc SC cKO mice exhibited significantly thinner myelin and pronounced deficits in motor performance and nerve conduction, accompanied by altered steady-state levels of autophagy-associated proteins and functional decline. Notably, Atg7 deletion in Galc SC cKO mice did not further increase macrophage abundance, suggesting that the worsened myelin phenotype occurs without additional macrophage recruitment at this stage. Together, these findings demonstrate that autophagy-associated changes occur early in KD and ATG7-dependent pathways play a protective role during disease progression. Modulating ATG7-dependent pathways may therefore warrant further investigation as a strategy to support myelin maintenance in KD and related lysosomal disorders.

title: Lattice Disorder in CuI Enables Filament-Free Transparent Memristors.
abstract: The realization of invisible neuromorphic electronics hinges on transparent memories that reconcile high optical transparency with stable analog tunability, which is a challenge unmet by conventional filamentary devices. Here, we introduce an alloyed Cu1- xAgxI halide transparent semiconductor with dual ionic-electronic character, which enables a filament-free switching platform. Ag+ incorporation induces lattice distortions within the γ-phase CuI matrix, expanding interstitial channels and lowering the migration barrier without phase transition. This activates room-temperature ion migration to dynamically modulate the p-type hole conductance. Asymmetric electrodes induce spatially distributed ion migration and interfacial modulation, avoiding localized metallic percolation. In situ TEM and EDS mapping confirm reversible Cu+/Ag+ redistribution without continuous conductive pathways. Pt/Cu1- xAgxI/Ag devices exhibit > 80% transparency, low-voltage readout, and > 2-year retention. They emulate synaptic plasticity and achieve high-accuracy handwritten digit recognition. Our findings establish a design strategy for transparent memristors, enabling reliable neuromorphic hardware via ionically mediated electronic transport.

title: Vagal sensing of altered gut microbiota links to externalizing behaviors.
abstract: Interoceptive brain responses triggered by intestinal microbiota influence mood-related behaviors such as anxiety and depression. Although genetic mutations can alter the gut microbiome, how alterations in the gut microbiome associated with host genetic variations relate to behavioral outcomes is not fully understood. We investigated how Sirtuin 3 (Sirt3) deficiency is linked to altered gut-brain interactions and mood-related behaviors. Gut microbiota composition and behavior were compared between Sirt3-knockout (KO) and wild-type (WT) mice. Cohousing and heterozygous littermate controls were used to assess microbiome-related contributions to behavioral differences. Transcriptomic profiling assessed region-specific gene expression in the limbic system. Metabolites in the nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS), potentially related to gut-brain vagal signaling, were analyzed. The role of the vagus nerve was further tested using subdiaphragmatic vagotomy in the Sirt3-KO mouse model, along with measurements of plasma choline levels in mice. Sirt3-KO mice displayed mood-related neurobehavioral changes and alterations in synaptic plasticity-related genes in the amygdala and the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), accompanied by alterations in gut microbiome composition. Elevated plasma choline levels in Sirt3-KO mice, together with reduced neurotransmitter-related metabolites (e.g., γ-aminobutyric acid [GABA] in the NTS), suggest that externalizing behaviors in Sirt3-KO mice involve vagus nerve-dependent gut-brain axis signaling. Consistent with the involvement of vagal signaling, vagotomized Sirt3-KO mice were similar to WT mice in these measures, including GABA levels in the NTS and synaptic plasticity-related changes in the amygdala and BNST. Our findings support a model in which host genetic variation-associated microbiome alterations are sensed through sustained gut-vagal signaling under non-stressed conditions, correlating with NTS neurotransmitter alterations and externalizing behavioral phenotypes.

title: Diabetes-Associated Cognitive Impairment: Pathophysiology and Emerging Therapies.
journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive impairment (DACI) is a common yet underrecognized condition, manifesting along a spectrum from mild cognitive impairment to dementia. DACI encompasses patients who develop vascular dementia (VaD) or Alzheimer's disease (AD) with diabetes as a risk factor; however, in certain patients, particularly those lacking clear VaD or AD features, diabetes may act as a primary driver of neurodegeneration. Mechanistically, DACI can be conceptualized as a neurovascular-metabolic disorder characterized by disruption of the neurovascular unit, impaired cerebral glucose metabolism, brain insulin resistance, and chronic neuroinflammation, contributing to small vessel disease, regional brain atrophy, and accelerated brain aging. In this narrative review, we synthesize current evidence on the clinical and imaging features of DACI, outline key mechanistic pathways linking diabetes to neurodegeneration, and discuss emerging therapeutic strategies, including GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors, with potential neuroprotective effects. Greater recognition of DACI as a neurovascular-metabolic entity may facilitate earlier identification, inform biomarker development, and guide future trials aimed at preserving cognitive function in individuals with diabetes.

title: Gonadotropin-Inhibitory Hormone (GnIH) and Its Receptor GPR147 Mediates Acute Stress-Induced Activation of the Locus Coeruleus-SAM Axis.
abstract: Gonadotropin-inhibitory hormone (GnIH, also known as RFamide-related peptide-3, RFRP-3) is a hypothalamic neuropeptide that regulates vertebrate reproduction via its receptor GPR147. Although GnIH is known to mediate stress-induced reproductive suppression, its role in broader stress responses remains unclear. This study investigated the fuction of GnIH in acute stress and evaluated the mechanisms by which GnIH regulates norepinephrine (NE) release and activates the locus coeruleus-sympathetic-adrenal medulla (LC-SAM) axis in mice. The results show that GnIH is co-localized and co-stored with NE in sympathetic nerve terminals and that it is associated with heightened LC-SAM axis activity induced by acute stressors. Central or peripheral administration of GnIH potentiated acute stress responses and activated the LC-SAM axis, accompanied by increased anxiety-like behaviors. Conversely, genetic ablation of GnIH or GPR147 attenuated acute stress-induced anxiety-like behaviors and LC-SAM axis activation. Mechanistically, both central and peripheral GnIH enhanced NE synthesis, transport and release. These findings indicate that GnIH mimics or augments endogenous NE signaling to activated the LC-SAM axis during acute stress. Pharmacological modulation of the GnIH/GPR147 system may represent a therapeutic approach for the inhibiting maladaptive stress responses and stress-related pathologies and infertility.

title: Mass Spectrometry Imaging Reveals Biodistribution and Biotransformation of Black Phosphorus.
abstract: Black phosphorus (BP) holds significant potential in biomedicine, biosensing, and phototherapy; however, its instability and the poor understanding of its in vivo fate have limited its applications. Here, we developed an integrated label-free mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) platform to investigate BP's in vivo distribution, transformation, clearance, and metabolism in tumor-bearing mice. We detected BPs and related nitrogen/oxygen-containing phosphorus (P) clusters in six organs and tumor tissues, revealing distinctive tissue distributions. BP and its degradation products primarily accumulated in the liver and spleen, with the liver showing a radial distribution pattern around hepatic lobules. Notably, BP and related clusters can cross the blood-brain barrier into brain parenchyma. We further establish the in vivo transformation and metabolic pathways of BPs. Cellular experiments confirmed that nitric oxide synthase (NOS)-mediated nitric oxide (NO) generation drives BP nitridation during its transformation and metabolism under physiological conditions. This work not only provides vital information for biomedical applications of BP, but also establishes a platform for understanding in vivo translocation and transformation of nanomaterials, aiding their biosafety and health impact assessments.

title: How the Brain Interprets Pain in Autistic People: Does Sex Matter?
abstract: While psychophysical studies suggest heightened pain sensitivity in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), the relationship between subjective pain experience and cortical neurophysiological responses and whether this relationship is sex-dependent, remains poorly understood. This cross-sectional two-group comparison study included 50 adults with Level 1 ASD and 52 age-, sex- and IQ-matched typically developing controls (TDC). Pain ratings and cortical contact heat-evoked potentials (CHEPs) were recorded in response to 52°C phasic heat stimuli. ANOVA and regression models assessed the effects of group, sex and pain ratings on CHEP amplitudes. Compared to TDC, autistic participants reported higher pain scores (p = 0.004) and had lower N2 amplitudes (p = 0.02). A significant Group × Sex interaction (p 0.05). Within-group correlation analyses in females showed a significant pain-N2 amplitude relationship in TDC (r = 0.734; p = 0.004) but not in autistic participants (r = 0.371; p = 0.192). Across groups and sexes, higher N2 amplitude values were associated with greater attention-to-detail autistic traits (p = 0.009). Our findings suggest a dissociation between subjective pain experience and cortical responses to nociceptive stimulation in autism, particularly among females, consistent with different salience-related or attentional pain processing. These results underscore the importance of considering sex and autism when interpreting pain-evoked cortical responses and challenge the assumption that pain-evoked potentials provide universally objective measures of pain. This study identifies sex-related differences in the relationship between subjective pain ratings and cortical responses to nociceptive stimulation in autistic and typically developing individuals. Autistic females showed particularly attenuated N2 amplitudes and a weaker correspondence between pain ratings and cortical responses, suggesting different salience-related or attentional processing of nociceptive stimuli. These findings highlight the importance of considering sex and autistic traits when interpreting pain-evoked cortical responses in autism.

title: Mitochondrial Protection and Neural Repair via ROS-Responsive Biomimetic Nanoparticles in Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH)-induced secondary brain injury is driven in part by oxidative stress, blood-brain barrier disruption, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuronal loss. Here, we developed a brain endothelial cell membrane-coated ROS-responsive biomimetic nanoplatform (NP@D+M) for co-delivery of the VDAC1 inhibitor DIDS and the mitochondrial fission inhibitor Mdivi-1. NP@D+M showed uniform size, preserved endothelial membrane proteins, and accelerated drug release under elevated H2O2. In ICH-like neuronal injury models, NP@D+M enhanced uptake, protected neurites, reduced LDH release and apoptosis, restored mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP production, and suppressed mitochondrial ROS. Mechanistically, NP@D+M disrupted aberrant LPAR1-VDAC1 interaction, inhibited mPTP opening, and restored mitochondrial homeostasis; LPAR1 gain- and loss-of-function experiments confirmed its role in the mitochondrial protective effect. Targeted metabolomics and single-cell transcriptomics further supported improved energy metabolism and attenuated injury-associated cellular responses. In vivo, NP@D+M crossed the BBB, accumulated in brain parenchyma, protected perihematomal neurons, improved mitochondrial function, and alleviated neurological and cognitive deficits without obvious systemic toxicity. These findings identify a LPAR1-VDAC1-mPTP-targeted nanotherapeutic strategy for mitochondrial protection and neural repair after ICH.

title: The weight of junk food: Smaller hippocampal, amygdala, and prefrontal volumes in adolescents-The Cogni-Action Project.
abstract: Most studies investigating diet-brain relationships in youth focus on single foods. Whether the joint consumption of multiple food groups is associated with neuroanatomy during adolescence remains largely unexplored, particularly outside high-income countries. In this cross-sectional study, 61 Chilean adolescents (11.6 ± 1.07 years; 42.6% girls) underwent T1-weighted MRI. Volumes of total gray matter, hippocampus, amygdala, and selected prefrontal regions were extracted. Dietary intake was assessed using the Global Food Quality Index questionnaire. Confounder-adjusted linear regressions examined individual food group-brain associations, with correction for multiple comparisons. Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) was used to identify multivariate food group-brain covariation with permutation-based inference. Univariate analyses showed a significant inverse association between pastry consumption and hippocampal volume (β = -0.402, 95% CI: -0.571 to -0.228, adjusted R2 = 0.34). CCA identified one significant multivariate mode linking higher unhealthy food consumption to brain volumes (r = -0.70, p = .008). Pastries, fried foods, and soft drinks showed the strongest contributions, whereas the corresponding brain variate was characterized by smaller hippocampal, amygdala, and anterior cingulate/prefrontal volumes. In conclusion, higher consumption of unhealthy food groups is associated with smaller limbic-prefrontal volumes in adolescents. Although causality cannot be inferred from these cross-sectional data, these findings highlight adolescence as a critical window for diet-brain health research.

title: scGEN: Leveraging an Adaptive Weighting Strategy for Challenging Cell Clustering in Single-Cell RNA-seq.
abstract: Recent advancements in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) have greatly enhanced our ability to dissect cellular heterogeneity. However, unsupervised clustering often struggles to identify transitional or developmental boundary cells, as existing methods rely on highly variable genes without considering expression levels, thereby overlooking subtle but crucial signals. To address this challenge, we developed a single-cell gene-aware embedded network (scGEN), which captures complex intercellular relationships. scGEN employs adaptive feature weighting and iterative fine-tuning to prioritize ambiguous or transitional cells with overlapping transcriptional profiles. Evaluation across eight distinct scRNA-seq datasets demonstrated that scGEN consistently outperformed nine leading clustering approaches. Additionally, scGEN generated refined assignments for approximately 10% of cells with ambiguous transcriptional profiles and revealed biologically meaningful differences, providing a more detailed view of cellular heterogeneity in the human fetal pituitary. Cell-cell communication analysis identified developmental signaling networks associated with the refined annotations, including a putative Pre.Gonado-like population detected at 7 weeks with prominent involvement in BMP, NOTCH, and extracellular matrix remodeling pathways. Furthermore, histological analysis of 6-8-week embryos provided orthogonal tissue-level support for early gonadotrope-lineage states and SOX2-GATA2-NR5A1 bridging populations. Together, these results highlight scGEN's ability to enhance cell-type assignments and detect subtle biological differences.

title: A machine learning approach to predicting high-risk irritability trajectories across the transition to adolescence.
abstract: Youth irritability, characterized as proneness to anger/frustration, is associated with negative mental health outcomes. This study identified irritability trajectories across the transition to early adolescence and applied machine learning to identify preadolescent predictors of irritability trajectories. Data are from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, a large longitudinal study that tracks youth development from preadolescence (n = 11,862, ages 8.92-11.08 years, M = 9.91, SD = 0.62). The baseline sample was 47.83% female (n = 5,680), 63.35% White, 15.74% Black, 12.07% Biracial or Multiracial, 2.32% Asian, and 20.30% Hispanic. Using parent-report youth irritability scores across four years, latent class growth analysis (LCGA) identified four distinct irritability trajectories: low stable (n = 8,692, 73.28%), high decreasing (n = 1,083, 9.13%), low increasing (n = 1,449, 12.22%), and high chronic (n = 638, 5.38%). Machine learning approaches generated predictive models for irritability trajectories, including baseline youth psychopathology, physical health, neurocognitive abilities, psychosocial environment, demographics, parent psychopathology, and brain structure metrics. The models demonstrated strong performance in detecting probability of being in the high chronic and low stable trajectories but poorer performance in classifying the irritability trajectories characterized by change. The most prominent predictors included youth externalizing and internalizing problems, parent psychopathology, and sleep problems. Findings provide insight into preadolescent predictors of irritability across a critical developmental period.

title: Low-Density Lipoprotein Receptor-Targeted Biomimetic Nanoplatform Suppresses Glioblastoma Stemness and Remodels Antitumor Immunity via Dual Metabolic Disruption.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains one of the most lethal malignancies because durable tumor control is constrained by limited brain-tumor drug exposure, metabolic plasticity, stem-like tumor states, and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. We developed apolipoprotein B fragment-decorated nanoparticles co-loaded with regorafenib and erythrodiol (ApoBf-R/E@NPs), a low-density lipoprotein receptor-oriented biomimetic nanoplatform that couples brain-tumor delivery with coordinated dual-drug exposure. Fixed-ratio combination-index analysis demonstrated synergy between the two agents. Regorafenib disrupts autophagy-associated nutrient salvage and restricts angiogenic support, whereas erythrodiol stabilizes ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 and depletes cellular cholesterol. These complementary perturbations converge on ATP depletion, mitochondrial dysfunction, and suppression of phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B and mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling. Across established and patient-derived GBM models, treatment broadly impaired tumor-cell survival while suppressing stemness-associated programs and reducing viability and tumorsphere persistence in patient-derived glioma stem-like cell cultures. Treatment also promoted an immunogenic cell death-associated tumor-cell state and antitumor immune remodeling. In immunocompetent GBM models, ApoBf-R/E@NPs showed preferential intracranial tumor-associated delivery, suppressed orthotopic and untreated distal tumor growth, and delayed postoperative regrowth, accompanied by systemic immune remodeling and expansion of memory-associated T-cell populations. These findings establish a blood-brain barrier-oriented nanodelivery strategy that couples complementary metabolic vulnerabilities to broad GBM control, stem-like compartment suppression, and antitumor immunity.
